The deliverable is a decisions.md entry with the argument attached and one test per getter showing its public predicate is sufficient — `contains`, `control_point_count`. This is `slice[i]` next to `len()`, and 110 call sites is not a lane's decision |

The four **cheap closures** that are in scope, all from §43.8: remove or deprecate
`Error::WhereALineMeetsATorusIsAQuartic` (`rcad-geom/src/error.rs`, constructed
nowhere in `src` — only two doc comments mention it); delete `rcad-topo`'s
`where_the_ray_meets` (`classify.rs:635`) in favour of
`rcad_geom::where_a_line_meets_a_surface`, which also closes
`Containment::CannotFireARayAtAFacesSurface` for a corner on the lattice; narrow
`StepFile`'s four methods that hand back unnameable types; and fix
`composite_wildcards.awk` to count uncovered variants rather than sites — noting
first, in writing, that `non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns` is the proper mechanism
and is unstable on the pinned 1.96.

### 44.10 How the work runs, and what green has to mean

**Lane 0 alone, then two waves.** At least three lanes at once, write sets named
before any lane starts, one deliverable per lane, stopping at about 45 minutes
(CLAUDE.md). **Every lane runs the `claim-audit` skill on its own deliverable
before reporting** — M5's lanes corrected each other four times while running and
its closing gate broke six more numbers none of them had caught. **One closing
gate re-derives every load-bearing number from the tree**, not from a lane's
report; a lane auditing itself is not a substitute.

`crates/rcad-topo/src/validate.rs` was wanted by four of five candidate lanes and
`error.rs` by three. The sequencing gives each exactly one owner at a time:

| stage | lane | owns |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | deserialize audit | `rcad-topo/src/{validate.rs,serialize.rs}`, `rcad-predicates/src/provenance.rs` |
| 1 | curved rounding | `rcad-topo/src/validate.rs`, `rcad-geom/src/{sphere,cylinder,cone,torus,lib}.rs` |
| 1 | interference | a new `rcad-topo` module, `rcad-topo/src/{error.rs,lib.rs}` |
| 1 | tangent direction | `rcad-topo/src/fuse/arrange.rs` |
| 1 | rate pinning | `rcad-step/tests/`, `justfile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
| 2 | two-step wires | `rcad-topo/src/{validate.rs,builder.rs,model.rs,error.rs,view.rs}` |
| 2 | the rest | as §44.4 lists |

**The one dependency to watch:** lane 0 and the curved-rounding lane both want
`validate.rs`. If lane 0's audit finds a third unguarded field it may want more of
that file, and wave one waits rather than merging around it.

**The curved-rounding lane's first act is a demonstration, not a number.** There
is **no curved analogue of `Plane::SIGNED_DISTANCE_ROUNDOFF`**
(`rcad-geom/src/plane.rs:77`), so the bound has to be derived and re-exported
before it can be spent. If a cylinder's representable-position error does not
decompose as cleanly as a plane's, **the item collapses and the lane reports
rather than inventing a number**. Whatever it publishes carries a §15.6 search
behind it, and it contradicts two doc comments that currently defer the curved
case — `validate.rs:1309-1313` and `rcad-step/src/refusal.rs:339-348` — both of
which go stale the day it lands.

**Verification. Green has to mean the corpus ran.**

- `mise exec -- just default` green, and **with `RCAD_STEP_CORPUS` unset the four
  corpus tests fail rather than skip**. Today all four print "skipping" and return
  green (`how_often_a_real_file_imports.rs:580`,
  `every_file_in_the_corpus_reads.rs:150`,
  `the_same_file_read_twice_by_two_readers.rs:281`,
  `a_real_file_written_out_and_read_back_is_the_same_solid.rs:433`), and nothing in
  `justfile` or `.github/workflows/ci.yml` sets the variable.
- **The 46 importing files are pinned by name, not by rate** — a rate hides which
  file moved — and the pinned list moves by the curved-rounding lane's own edit.
  `how_often_a_real_file_imports.rs:337` asserts only `!files.is_empty()` today;
  1 of 323 would pass it.
- `two_solids_described_at_the_same_place_are_still_called_a_valid_model`
  (`building_a_solid_out_of_faces.rs:358`) **fails** — criterion 8 landed. §19's
  shape.
- A `Model` deserialized with an infinite or negative `Approximation` magnitude is
  refused at the door, from bytes, and so is one carrying a non-finite vertex
  coordinate. The two fuzz targets assert it rather than walking past it.
- The `ModelData` asymmetry table is published, whatever it turns up.
- A tangent plane-and-cylinder pair fuses, or refuses for a reason that is true,
  checked against `degenerate_curved_fuses.rs:1539-1547`.
- `a_plate_bounded_by_an_arc_and_its_chord` builds and validates.
- The `validate.rs:436` skip's hit count over the existing corpora is published,
  whatever it is. Thousands makes it a correctness lane; zero means two doc
  comments disagree in the tree, and **that is the finding**.
- `just check-enums`, `just check-wildcards`, `just deny`, and the soak at
  `RCAD_SOAK_FACTOR=200`, all as M5 left them.

### 44.11 Corrections this section makes

Six, four of them to §42 and §43 and two to this unit's own planning. They are
here rather than as edits to the sections they correct, per §43.7's convention.

1. **Option C needs no new mechanism.** §42.9 and §43.8 item 12 both price it as
   *"a new `Cause` variant and a `Measures` arm"*, and
   `rcad-step/src/refusal.rs:347-348` repeats the first half in a doc comment —
   *"§42.9's option C, with a `Cause` of its own"*. `Cause::ImportedUncertainty`
   and `Measures::Length` both already exist, and the `Cause` is constructed
   nowhere in production. §44.6 has the demonstration. C is **one decision**, and
   that doc comment is a third place the corrected price has to reach.
2. **§42.9's D trigger was never scored, and §43.8 item 12 replaced D with C
   without saying so.** §44.6 scores it: not fired today, live after this unit's
   two lanes land.
3. **The two-step wire is bigger than §43.8 item 1 makes it sound.** It is **two
   independent length rules in two files** — `check_the_steps_close`
   (`rcad-topo/src/builder.rs:335-338`, raising `Error::ADraftWireIsTooShort`) and
   `check_wire_closes` (`validate.rs:304-309`, raising `Invalid::WireTooShort`,
   whose message says "at least three") — plus `winding_of` (`validate.rs:1347`,
   called from `check_flat_face`), which reads a wire's winding off its corner
   polygon so a face bounded by two half-circles sweeps exactly zero and cannot be
   told from a hole, plus `Model::add_wire_of_steps` (`model.rs:471`),
   `check_touched_wire` (`:560`), `wire_closes_on_one_edge` (`:587`) and
   `WireView::closes_on_one_edge` (`view.rs:690`). The reuse is already in the
   tree: `check_flat_face` skips one-edge wires at `validate.rs:928-931`, which is
   the same shape of exception a two-step wire needs.
4. **"The four curved surface files carry only a predicate name constant" is
   false.** Each also carries a private `SIDE_OF_*_ERROR_BOUND`
   (`sphere.rs:290`, `cylinder.rs:443`, `cone.rs:511`, `torus.rs:494`). The
   conclusion survives — those are the sign predicate's own filter bound, in the
   predicate's units, not a position error in a length, and none is re-exported —
   but the sentence as written understates what is already there, and the lane
   should start from those consts rather than from nothing.
5. **"The pinned count moves from 46 toward ~136" is an upper bound, not a
   projection, and the KiCad half of it is 134.** §43.5's 88 is drawn from the
   **161** KiCad files with a corner off a curved face, not from the **153** whose
   *first* refusal it was, so at most 88 files have their first blocker removed and
   each may then meet a second. The 2 NIST files in the 90 are in a separate family
   with its own count. **What the lane must report is the measured number and the
   filenames, not a target.**
6. **§43.5's KiCad refusal table does not sum, and its NIST column does.** The
   table says it counts each file once, named by what stopped it first. NIST:
   16 + 15 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 2 = **44**, exactly the family. KiCad:
   153 + 59 + 29 + 13 + 8 + 23 = **285** against 323 − 46 = **277** refused, over
   by **8** — the size of exactly one row, *a corner is not on the plane of the arc
   it ends on*. Either that row is not a first-refusal count or one row is eight
   too large. **This gate cannot re-derive it**: the corpus is not in the tree and
   `RCAD_STEP_CORPUS` is unset, which is §44.10's first verification line and is
   itself the reason the discrepancy survived a closing gate. **The rate-pinning
   lane settles it** when it publishes a per-file refusal reason, and §44.6's
   trigger is written as a range because of it.

### 44.12 What this gate does not know, and the prediction

- **Whether a cylinder's representable-position error decomposes like a plane's.**
  The whole curved-rounding item rests on it, and it is a demonstration nobody has
  run. §44.10 makes the lane's first act to settle it and its second to report if
  it does not.
- **What the `validate.rs:436` skip costs.** `error.rs:558-578` documents the fuse
  producing exactly the shape `holds.rs:400-402` abandons — a crossing cut at two
  corners leaving two arcs with the same two ends — while the only test of the
  check (`validate.rs:2013-2058`) has a doc saying *"no builder makes this and the
  fuse will not"*. One of those two sentences is wrong and instrumentation says
  which.
- **Whether interference has an answer that is not quadratic.** `Bounds::overlap`
  (`fuse/bake.rs:171-181`) is a box-level broad phase and `cuts.rs:78-82` is its
  current caller, so the shape exists; what nobody has costed is the narrow phase
  for the two cases roadmap §7.4 (`docs/roadmap.md:520-521`) names — fully
  contained, and touching but not overlapping.

**The prediction, recorded before the work and to be scored at this unit's closing
gate** (§30.2's cheaper half; §43.10's prediction is inherited alongside it).
§12.1's lesson — the money goes to code that was already written and looked
finished — is bet on for a third time: **the money goes to the two-step wire, not
to the curved rounding.** §43.8 item 1 reads as one rule and §44.11 item 3 already
found it is two rules in two files plus a winding question that has no answer for a
face bounded by two arcs; the curved rounding, by contrast, has a worked precedent
sitting in `validate.rs` that let 4147 of 4174 refused corners through. The second
guess is that **lane 0's audit finds a third unguarded field**, because it found
its second during planning and stopped only because planning ended. The third, and
the one this gate would most like to be wrong about, is that **criterion 8 goes
unstarted for a third unit running.**

disagree, the gate's number stands and the lane's is kept beside it, because the

|---|---|---|
| **KiCad imported** | 46 / 323 = 14.2% | **97 / 323 = 30.0%** |
| NIST imported | 0 / 44 | 0 / 44 |
| control | 88 / 88 | 88 / 88 |

Two sentences, and the split between them is the whole of §45.2:

- **A file whose corners are as close as an `f64` can put them is no longer
  refused for being off** — §44.3's first sentence, **+50 files**.
- **A face bounded by an arc and its chord is a face** — §44.3's second, **+1**.

Four things the corpus does not measure landed beside them: criterion 8 exists
(`overlap.rs`), a `Model` off the wire can no longer switch off the certified

### 45.2 §44.3 priced the second sentence at 75 files. It is worth one.

Of the 75 files whose *first* refusal was the wire rule, **1 now imports and 74
meet a second blocker immediately** — 63 into the curved-face bucket, 11 into

before-rows against 270 after-rows to get it, rather than trusting the totals.

**§44.11 item 5 was written about the curved item and governs both.** It says a

worth, never a projection**. Scored:

|---|---|---|
| curved writer's rounding | 88 | **50** |
| the two-step wire | 75 | **1** |

Both of §44's headline file counts were upper bounds wearing a projection's

future count of this shape — including the 68 B-spline files, which are the next

### 45.3 The refusal name is not the reason, so option D cannot be scored

§44.6 wrote its option-D trigger as a fraction *"so it can fire"* and deferred
scoring to this gate. **The gate refuses to score it, and it is right to.**

| | KiCad refused | refused for a miss > 1 spacing | trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| as published | 226 | 128 | 56.6% — **fires** |
| less the 57 relabelled | 226 | 71 | 31.4% — **does not fire** |

`SolidBuilder::build` failing for *any* reason sends `brep.rs` to
`a_corner_provably_off_a_curved_face`, and if a bare exact `side_of` finds any
corner off any curved face, that name wins ahead of the real reason. Since the
curved lane landed, **that criterion is strictly stricter than the one
`Model::validate` now uses**, because it carries no `NEAREST_F64_POINT_ROUNDOFF`
slack. `brep.rs` is not in this unit's diff; the divergence was made by changing
`validate` around it.

**The demonstration, which no lane had:** of the 63 ex-wire files that landed in
that bucket, **0 are inside one coordinate spacing**, against 40 of 168 (24%)
for the corpus as a whole. A bucket of genuine corner misses does not have a
zero there.

**So the first thing the next unit owes is a first-refusal count that `brep.rs`
has not overwritten.** Until then no statement about option D is available in
either direction, and §44.6's own arithmetic is unusable for the reason in §45.4.

### 45.4 §44.11 item 6, settled — and it was three mistakes, not one

§44.11 item 6 recorded §43.5's KiCad table as `153+59+29+13+8+23 = 285` against
277 refused, over by 8, and could not tell which row was wrong. Two lanes gave
different answers and both were right about different objects.

1. **The sum.** The measured tail at `b3e5670` is `6+3+2+2+1+1 = 15`, and
   §43.5's own text reads "… `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` 1, **and 8 more**".
   `23 = 15 + 8`, where that 8 is the arc-plane row already listed above it.
   `153+59+29+13+8+15 = 277` exactly. **A double-count in the prose; the tree's
   counts were always sound.**
2. **The row.** It is also not a first-refusal count, for §45.3's reason. Both
   things are true at once.
3. **A third quantity nobody had checked.** §44.6 argues from *"161 KiCad files
   with a corner off a curved face"* exceeding *"the 153 whose first refusal it
   was"* by 8. **There is no such set of 161.** `corner_misses_in_spacings` is
   pushed for **both** corner-miss variants, so the reported 161 is `153 + 8` —
   the same 8 a third time. §44.6's 65–73 range and its "50% to 56%" rest on it.

The lesson is narrower than "check the arithmetic": three different sentences in
two sections all reused one number without asking what population it came from.

### 45.5 The `ModelData` table — §44.5 deliverable 4, published here

§44.5 asked for this table and §44.10 made publishing it a verification line.
The lane produced it in its report and **it never reached the tree**; the gate
caught that the line was unmet. It is published here. "Guard" means: does
something refuse a bad value **on the deserialize path**, which runs
`check_keys_resolve`, `check_nothing_is_used_more_than_once` and
`check_shape_is_possible`, and nothing else.

| field / payload | serde | guard at the door | what a hostile value cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ModelData.scale` | `try_from` | yes — `Scale::new` | — |
| the seven `SlotMap`s | derive | partly — slotmap refuses ≥ `u32::MAX` slots and rebuilds `num_elems` and the free list itself | — |
| `VertexData.point` | `from` — cannot refuse | **now yes** — `VertexNotFinite` | every predicate downstream asked about a coordinate that is not a number |
| `VertexData.approximation` | was plain derive | **now yes** — `try_from` | **an infinite magnitude switched the certified check off**: `not_provably_off` keeps any magnitude `> 0.0`, widening the corner to an interval reaching every surface, and `validate` returned `Ok` on a solid whose corners are nowhere near its faces |
| `EdgeData.start/end` | derive | yes — `check_keys_resolve` | — |
| `EdgeData.run` | derive | leaves yes — every `Surface` and `Picker` arm is `try_from` | a run naming a curve the edge is not on is caught in `validate` only, and correctly so: it needs a `Policy` and a predicate |
| `EdgeData.approximation` | was plain derive | **now yes** | as vertex |
| `CoedgeData.edge` / `.orientation` | derive | yes | — |
| `WireData.steps` | derive | keys yes; shape yes; **multiplicity now yes** | see §45.6 |
| `FaceData.surface` | `try_from` | yes | — |
| `FaceData.wires` | derive | keys yes; non-empty yes; **multiplicity now yes** | see §45.6 |
| `FaceData.approximation` | was plain derive | **now yes** | as vertex |
| `ShellData.faces` | derive | keys, `loc` and `orient` yes; **multiplicity now yes** | see §45.6 |
| `SolidData.shells` | derive | as `ShellData.faces` | see §45.6 |
| `Model.worst_approximation` | not stored | recomputed | a file cannot lie about it |
| `Model.id` | not stored | minted per read | old keys are refused against the new model |

`Point` and `Vector` keep `#[serde(from)]` deliberately (§44.5): a fallible
branch on every coordinate in the kernel is a real cost, and finiteness is a
condition a sweep already implements.

### 45.6 The hole that was not a field

§44.12 predicted lane 0's audit would find a third unguarded **field**. It found
something worse and of a different kind: **nothing at the door counted how many
times an entity is used.**

A cube whose second face names the first face's wire read back cleanly —
`check_keys_resolve` passed, `check_shape_is_possible` passed — and
`Index::rebuilt_from`'s `insert` **silently gave the wire to whichever face was
written last**. Six faces, one wire each, and the index disagreeing with the data
it was built from before anything asked a question. `Model::validate` caught it;
`validate` is not on that path. Found by a lane, reproduced independently by the
gate, and closed last.

**Where the check runs is the part worth recording.** §44.5's rule said it
belongs in `check_shape_is_possible`, and it does not: that is a method on
`Model` and needs `self.index()`, so it can only run *after* the index exists —
and the index is what the count protects. It runs in `Deserialize` beside
`check_keys_resolve`, before `from_parts`. Four counts — coedges by wires, wires
by faces, faces by shells, shells by solids — one `SecondaryMap` each, O(n).
`rebuilt_from`'s two inserts now **assert unconditionally** rather than
`debug_assert`, because by then the bytes are vetted, so a second claimant is a
broken internal invariant, and a `debug_assert` is absent in exactly the build
where a user opens a stranger's file.

**The symmetric hole is still open.** `Invalid::Orphan` — a face in no shell, a
wire on no face, a coedge in no wire, a shell in no solid — qualifies under the
same rule and is still not at the door.

### 45.7 Three measurements that changed a verdict

**The skip.** §44.10 asked for the hit count of
`check_which_side_of_its_trimming_each_curved_face_lies_on`'s `continue`, and
§44.12 framed the answer as a fork: *thousands makes it a correctness lane, zero
means two doc comments disagree.* It fires **33 004** times — and it is still not
a correctness lane, because in **32 965 of 33 005 raises the face had no whole
closed trimming at all**. A per-edge rewrite recovers **40 face-visits across the
entire suite**, and that 40 is identical in debug, in release and in the lane's
own log while the percentage moves with the denominator. Neither doc comment is
wrong: they are about different objects, and §44.12 read them as contradicting.
What survives is sharper — *"the fuse will not make a straddling face"* is an
unreachability claim **the sweep is in no position to have tested**, since it is
skipped on 96.1% of the fuse's own curved face-visits. The real finding is a
coverage number nobody had: **3.90%** over the fuse's own swept curved output,
2.18% over KiCad. The remedy is a second invariant that can speak about an arc,
and that is milestone-sized.

**A number that went stale inside the unit.** The same lane measured NIST at
**0** and was right. By the final tree it is **204**, because `door3-twostep`
let two NIST files build far enough to reach the skip while still being refused
at import. The gate proved it by rebuilding the probe at `d680434` and
reproducing the lane's `0` exactly. **A lane's number can be true when taken and
false when merged**, which is the argument for a gate re-deriving at the final
tree, demonstrated rather than asserted.

**The round-trip charge.** §43.2 scored criterion 12 unmet and cited
`fuse/select.rs:1045`. That site round-trips through a surface's *own two
coordinates* and is charged correctly; the uncharged trip was in
`rcad-topo/src/mesh.rs`, which §44.4 filed under "the mesher" while `rcad-mesh`
contains no `transformed` call at all. And **`18·ε` was never a claim about this
operation** — it is `Isometry::POINT_ROUNDOFF`, what the deflection floor
charges, so §41.8's "fourteen times short" compared two unrelated constants. The
derived cost is `36·ε·L` for a ball (a centre) and `72·ε·L` for a pipe, cone or
ring (a point *and* a direction); worst measured `4·ε·L`. A real gap, of the same
order as the charge rather than 14× it.

### 45.8 The predictions

| prediction | score |
|---|---|
| §44.12 #1 — the money goes to the two-step wire, not the curved rounding | **not borne out by cost, right about shape.** The curved lane is larger by insertions and paid 50 files; the two-step paid 1. But the two-step lane was the messier: two rules in two files, a winding exception, a fixture wrong since it was written, and a mesh gap it could not close |
| §44.12 #2 — lane 0's audit finds a third unguarded field | **wrong as worded, right in spirit** — see §45.6. It is a multiplicity, not a field |
| §44.12 #3 — criterion 8 goes unstarted a third unit | **wrong, and the gate got the outcome it wanted** |
| §43.10, inherited — corner slop first, criterion 8 second, the fuse's unjudged `expect`s third | **first two done, third untouched for the third unit running.** `.expect(` in `crates/rcad-topo/src/fuse/` is **147** at both ends of the unit, 30 of them production. `arrange.rs` was rewritten by +328 lines without adding or judging one |

**§12.1's lesson holds a third time in a new form.** The money did not go where
either the plan or the last gate said. It went to work nobody had scheduled at
all: a wrong region meshed silently round a ball's pole, a door that let a
self-contradicting model through, and a fixture that had been inside out since
the day it was written. All three were found by *removing a restriction* and
seeing what the tree did next.

### 45.9 Claims that did not survive

Every lane ran `claim-audit` on its own work and corrected itself — five
sentences in one lane, four in another, three in a third. Those are in the
commits. What a lane auditing itself could not see, and the gate found:

- **A §15.6 search with two assertions that cannot fail.** The headline
  constant's own test presented four checks per bracket as independent; two were
  tautologies (`spacing ≤ budget` holds for any point and names no surface).
  Now sorted explicitly into what tests the size, what proves the search is not
  vacuous, and what is bookkeeping — **and a search that can actually fail was
  built**: Pythagorean quadruples put a point exactly on a ball, pipe, cone or
  ring with no arithmetic, one IEEE division rounds it, and the distance moved
  is compared with the budget. Worst shares 0.508 to 0.584, and **all four
  surfaces fail when the constant is halved.**
- **A doc claiming a tighter ceiling than its code asserted** — `mesh.rs` said
  `36·ε·L` and asserted `72·ε·L`. Charging each surface its own ceiling
  uncovered what the shared number hid: **all 480 ball faces stray exactly
  zero**, because `add_ball` stores its sphere on the origin of its own
  placement and `M⁻¹(M(origin))` cancels to the bit. The ball's half of a
  "two roads must differ" test had been comparing a road with itself.
- **A ratchet that reset its own instrument.** `wildcard_arms` 90 → 87 reads as
  three arms going away and is one: measured both scans on both trees, the
  composite half moved entirely because it started counting uncovered variants
  instead of sites. The four bridging rows are now in the `justfile`.

### 45.10 What stands in the door now

**Correctness, in the order a next unit should take them:**

1. **A first-refusal count `brep.rs` has not overwritten** (§45.3). Everything
   published about why files are refused depends on it, and option D cannot be
   scored without it.
2. **`Invalid::Orphan` at the door** (§45.6) — the same rule, the other half.
3. **The fuse's 30 production `expect`s**, unjudged for a third unit. §43.3
   demonstrated eleven such clauses reachable with caller data in one milestone;
   `arrange.rs` grew by a third this unit without any of them being looked at.

**Named limits and gaps, each with its demonstration in the tree:**

- **A plane resting on a pipe leaves that crossing with no direction.**
  `∇S × ∇Q` is exactly the zero vector along the tangent ruling. Four families
  of fix are ruled out at the refusal site in `arrange.rs`, including the sharp
  one: storing a direction on `Crossing` is **necessary but not sufficient**,
  because `det(∇S, ∇Q₁, ∇Q₂)` vanishes identically once `∇Q₁ ∥ ∇S` and the
  curvature fallback dies with it. Both derivatives the engine takes are blind.
- **A quarter arc contributes no corner at `as_coarse_as_a_mesh_gets`**, so a
  plate bounded by one will not mesh. `a_plate_bounded_by_a_quarter_arc_and_its_chord_still_will_not_mesh`
  is the only `#[ignore]` in the suite and names its own fix. **Nothing runs
  `--ignored`**, so it will stay quiet after the fix lands.
- **A face bounded by two half-circles** sweeps exactly zero winding and is
  refused. A gap: the runs carry the answer and nothing reads them.
- **The writer has no `SURFACE_CURVE`** for the circle where a flat face meets a
  round one, so 52 of the 97 importing files do not round-trip. Nothing that
  used to round-trip stopped.
- **The sweep sees 3.90% of the fuse's own curved output** (§45.7).

**A prediction, for whoever scores it.** §44.2 dropped the a-priori criteria
list and replaced it with a verification list in which every line names
something in the tree that changes state. That worked: three of §44.10's lines
were found unmet or unmeetable by a gate, and one of them — the `ModelData`
table — would have been recorded as done on a lane's word. **So the guess is
that the next unit's biggest loss is again a number that was true when a lane
took it and false when the unit closed**, because that failure mode survived
this unit's own precautions and was caught only by re-running at the final tree.
The second guess is that `brep.rs` turns out to have been distorting the
refusal tables for longer than this unit, and that some earlier published rate
moves when it is fixed.

## 46. The cut — the unit after the door, recorded 2026-09-03

*Written before any lane was dispatched, in §44's shape and not §42's. Every file
and line it cites was checked against the tree at `ef2b096`. It puts the
corrections first, because a lane that reads a stale price scopes itself wrong on
its first day.*

### 46.1 The name, and what the unit is

Called **the cut**. Roadmap §12 keeps M6 for local operations, per §44.1's
precedent and principle 6.

The name comes from §43.10's verdict on the kernel: *"a kernel that can build a
shape and cannot cut it is a modeller you can put things into and not take things
out of."* Cone and torus faces can be built, validated, measured, meshed and
classified. They cannot be fused with much, and the suite pins that as expected
behaviour — `how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs:316` asserts
`AFrustumAgainstABar` at nothing answered, and
`how_often_a_fuse_with_a_torus_refuses.rs:286` asserts *every* bend family there.

**The sentence the unit earns:**

> **A plane cuts a cone in a parabola, a hyperbola and a ruling, and the kernel
> can draw all three.**

The fuse clause — *and a frustum can be cut by a block* — is added **only if the
fuse lane lands**. "96 of 96" is a downstream count nobody has measured against a
fix, and §45.2 scored two numbers of exactly that shape at 88 → 50 and 75 → 1.

### 46.2 Planning re-priced the headline twice, both times downward

It looked like roadmap §13 row 1, the named schedule risk. It is not.

1. **It is not missing cone×cone SSI.** `intersect` already computes plane×cone
   and refuses two of the conic kinds that pair can produce.
2. **§43.6 had already written the consumer down** — `ACrossingThatIsAParabola` /
   `ACrossingThatIsAHyperbola`, *"consumer: a frustum against an upright block,
   96 of 96 refusals"*.

So the headline is a conic-classification gap inside a working function.

**The refusal is decided twice, independently, by the same polynomial.**
`E = (n·w)² − slope²·‖n×w‖²` is computed in `intersect.rs:1680-1704` for naming
and again through `Exact` in `walk.rs:1115-1122` for drawing. One
`match (apex_is_on_the_plane, leaning)` at `intersect.rs:1700-1712` has four arms
and answers one:

| arm | today |
|---|---|
| `(false, Pos)` | the ellipse — `NamedRun::the_whole_of(RightRoundWhereItsFacesCross)` |
| `(false, Zero)` | `Err(ACrossingThatIsAParabola)` — `intersect.rs:1706` |
| `(false, Neg)` | `Err(ACrossingThatIsAHyperbola)` — `intersect.rs:1707` |
| `(true, Zero)` | `Err(APlaneTouchingAConeAlongOneOfItsRulings)` — `intersect.rs:1711` |

**Naming needs no new `EdgeRun` variant.** `PartOfWhereItCrosses { and, picked_by }`
carries a parabola — it lies wholly in one nappe, so the half-space through the
apex square to the axis picks it — and each hyperbola branch, one per nappe. This
is fix (b) of the three `error.rs:335-348` already enumerates, and the one it
names shortest. It is also the only one that avoids adding a variant to a
`#[non_exhaustive]` enum that is `Serialize`/`Deserialize` and matched across two
crates.

**Drawing is the blocker, not naming.** `walk.rs`'s `Conic { centre, across, and,
size }` evaluates as `centre + across·cos θ + and·sin θ` (`walk.rs:787-801`). A
parabola has no centre and no semi-axes, so `where_a_plane_cuts_a_cone` cannot
return one and `walk` has no arm that consumes anything else. **The lane's real
cost is a second curve representation beside `Conic` and the walker arms that read
it** — and the lane demonstrates that choice rather than citing §43.6, for the
reason in §46.3.

### 46.3 Three corrections, before any lane reads them

**1. §43.6 and `error.rs:392-395` price the ruling wrongly.** Both say removing
`APlaneTouchingAConeAlongOneOfItsRulings` is *"one signature change in
`how_a_crossing_runs`"*. It is not one, and it is not a signature change.
`how_a_crossing_runs` (`arrange.rs:2914`) **already takes `run: &NamedRun`**. The
write sites are four, in three files: `intersect.rs:1711`, `walk.rs:1119`, the
cone arms of `a_plane_along_a_pipes_axis` (`arrange.rs:3057`, `Cylinder`-only and
`false` for every `Cone` pair) and `a_pair_that_crosses_in_a_conic`
(`arrange.rs:3023`) — and `assemble.rs:1967-1990`, whose doc says *"a cone never
reaches here running straight"* and which answering the ruling falsifies.

This is a price asserted and never checked, which is the failure mode CLAUDE.md's
rule about claims exists for. It matters because §43.6's endorsement of fix (b) in
§46.2 sits two lines from the claim that just failed, so it is not evidence.

**2. §45.10 understates the writer.** It says the writer has no `SURFACE_CURVE`,
so 52 of 97 importing files do not round-trip. The writer emits three things
(`write.rs:400-460`): a `LINE` for an open plane×plane edge, a `CIRCLE` for a
closed plane×cylinder edge whose plane is exactly square to the axis, and a `LINE`
for a cylinder seam. **Every other pair — plane×sphere, plane×cone, plane×torus,
cylinder×sphere, sphere×sphere — is `Err(ACurveTheFacesEitherSideOfItDoNotName)`.**
A ball that imports cleanly cannot be written out at all. Still deferred; now
described correctly.

**3. Two of the five surfaces are unreachable through the front door.**
`crates/rcad/src/lib.rs` re-exports `Plane`, `Sphere`, `Cylinder`, `Surface`,
`BSplineCurve` and `BSplineSurface` — but **not `Cone`, not `Torus`**, and not
`SIDE_OF_CONE`/`SIDE_OF_TORUS`. A facade caller can match `Surface::Cone(c)` and
cannot name `c`'s type, construct one, or build a cone face. This is on no
previous list — not §45.10, not §43.8, not §41.11 — and three closing gates
passed over it.

### 46.4 How the unit is scored

§44.2's change is kept: no a-priori criteria list, one closing gate, and a
verification list in which every line names something in the tree that changes
state.

Two rules the unit adopts from §45's findings:

- **The rate is reported and never targeted, and no file-count projection is
  published.** §45.2 demonstrated twice that a count of files a blocker stops
  *first* is an upper bound, not a projection. The 68 B-spline files are not
  priced here.
- **The gate's budget is reserved before the first lane starts.** §45.7 showed a
  lane's number can be true when taken and false when merged; §45.8 predicts that
  is how this unit loses too. A unit that spends its budget on lanes and gates on
  fumes gets exactly that.

**One verification line is worth naming here**, because it is the one that decides
whether the headline was right. `how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs:310`
asserts `refused > 0` for `AFrustumAgainstACornerUpCube |
APointedConeAgainstACornerUpCube`, and its own comment says *"re-derive the number
rather than relax it"*. Closing the hyperbola could take those families to none
refused and break it. **If it does not break, that is the finding**: the hyperbola
was not what refused them, and the fuse lane's price is wrong.

### 46.5 What the unit carries in, and what stays out

From §45.10, as opening lanes: the first-refusal count `brep.rs` has not
overwritten; `Invalid::Orphan` at the door; and the fuse's 30 production
`expect`s — unjudged for a third unit, and taken **before** the geometry lanes
because the cut has to touch `arrange.rs` and `assemble.rs`, which is where 29 of
the 30 live.

| out | why |
|---|---|
| **fillets** | §44.7's re-pricing is accepted — criterion 8 exists now, so it is one lane's machinery and not two — but a blend built on an operation that refuses its own primitives is built on sand |
| **another import-rate push** | cannot be honestly scored until the first-refusal count lands (§45.3) |
| **the writer** | §46.3 item 2. Deferred, described correctly |
| **option C, healing the 76** | one decision — *what is an imported corner's slop?* — but §45.3 means we cannot currently say which files are really in that bucket. Answered at the next gate, against the corrected table |
| **torus×curved, three-surface meets** | roadmap §13 row 1. Taking it in the same unit is how it eats the schedule |
| **`CannotWorkOutHowBigACrossingIs` at radius `1e-200`** | §43.8 item 4. A dynamic-range question; it belongs with the scaling work |

### 46.6 The decision rule for the first-refusal count, committed before the number is read

§45.2 and §45.4 both record numbers read after the fact and used three ways. The
rule is written first so there is nothing to read motivatedly:

- The curved-corner bucket **shrinks by more than half** once `brep.rs` stops
  overwriting → the published refusal tables were distorted, §45's second
  prediction scores as right, and option C is answered at the next gate against
  the corrected bucket.
- It **barely moves** → §45.3's relabelling was noise, and option D's trigger is
  scored on the spot: it fires or it does not, on the published number.
- **Either way**, no projection is published.

Both branches are survivable, which is the point.

### 46.7 The unit is renamed *the six arms*, and the sentence changes with it

§46.1 through §46.6 were written before the plan was grilled. The grilling read
the tree four more times and moved eight decisions; what follows corrects the
sections above, and where they disagree, these win.

**The name.** *The cut* is held for the unit where the conic-drawing half lands,
if it lands. This unit is **the six arms**, after the match it is named for. A
title is a claim, and §45.2's rule — a headline priced before a lane runs is
priced twice too high — applies to titles as much as to file counts. The unit's
guaranteed deliverable is in `rcad-geom`; the fuse clause sits behind a spike, a
lane and a merge.

**The sentence.** §46.1's is replaced by:

> **`where_a_plane_and_a_cone_cross` answers all six of its arms, and the kernel
> can draw every shape a plane cuts a cone in.**

Falsifiable by counting: open `intersect.rs:1702-1714` and see whether any arm
still returns `Err`. If the spike in §46.10 fails, the sentence keeps its drawing
clause for the two straight shapes and says plainly which two it lost and why.
The fuse clause — *and a frustum can be cut by a block* — is added only against
the assertion §46.9 pins, never against a printed number.

### 46.8 Six corrections, and the first of them is to a correction

Three of these correct §46.3, which was itself written as the corrections
section. That is worth saying out loud rather than filing quietly.

**1. §46.3 item 1 mis-priced the very mis-pricing it was correcting.** It said
the ruling's write sites are *"four, in three files"*. They are in **one file**:
the definition `arrange.rs:2914`, the callers `:1043` and `:4342`, the `HowItRuns`
enum `:452-464` and its `closes()` helper `:466-470`. §43.6 and
`error.rs:392-395` were wrong about the word (*"one signature change"* — it
already takes `run: &NamedRun`), and the correction was wrong about the scale, in
the same pass that produced three re-pricings the other way. A price nobody
checks stays wrong however many times it is rewritten.

**2. The match has six arms, not four, and it already answers two.** §46.2's
table lists four. `intersect.rs:1702-1714` also carries `(true, Pos)` →
`TouchAtOnePoint` at the apex, which is **answered**, and `(true, Neg)` →
`TwoLinesThroughAConesApexAreOneCurveThroughItself`, which is **refused and on no
previous list**. Two answered, four refused:

| arm | today |
|---|---|
| `(false, Pos)` | the ellipse — `the_whole_of(RightRoundWhereItsFacesCross)` |
| `(false, Zero)` | `Err(ACrossingThatIsAParabola)` |
| `(false, Neg)` | `Err(ACrossingThatIsAHyperbola)` |
| `(true, Pos)` | `TouchAtOnePoint` at the apex |
| `(true, Zero)` | `Err(APlaneTouchingAConeAlongOneOfItsRulings)` |
| `(true, Neg)` | `Err(TwoLinesThroughAConesApexAreOneCurveThroughItself)` |

**3. §45.10 understates the writer** — as §46.3 item 2 already said, kept here so
the corrected list is one list. Deferred, described correctly.

**4. `Cone` and `Torus` cannot be named through the front door, and five
`SIDE_OF_*` bounds for surfaces the kernel supports were never published.**
§46.3 item 3 found the first half. The second half is that of six `SIDE_OF_*`
constants — `cone.rs:18`, `torus.rs:15`, `plane.rs:15`, `sphere.rs:16`,
`cylinder.rs:18`, `half_space.rs:12` — `crates/rcad/src/lib.rs:357` re-exports
**one**. A facade caller cannot name the bound its own results were certified
against for any surface but a half-space.

**5. `brep.rs` overwrites the real refusal twice, and a published column measures
the wrong corner.** `brep.rs:600-626` substitutes
`a_corner_provably_off_a_curved_face` (`:643-675`, which takes nothing derived
from `why` and rescans every non-planar face), and when that finds nothing falls
through to `a_corner_provably_off_the_plane_of_its_own_arc` (`:698`), whose own
rustdoc at `:680-697` calls it a rounding artefact of how the plane is stored.
The corpus report's `miss={...} spacings` column
(`how_often_a_real_file_imports.rs:409-419, :688`) is computed from the
**substituted** refusal — a measurement of a corner that may have had nothing to
do with the failure. §45.3 said the refusal name is not the reason; this says the
number beside the name is not the reason's either.

**6. `Invalid::Orphan` already exists** — `error.rs:950`, raised in five places
in the full sweep (`validate.rs:179, :291, :318, :431, :578`). What is missing is
a check at the deserialize door, not a variant. Worth a correction because a lane
that did not know would have budgeted for one.

### 46.9 The headline family was unasserted, and is pinned before any lane runs

`how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs` asserted every family in its table
except the one the unit rests on. `AFrustumAgainstABlock` was *"reported, not
judged"*: a lane could have taken it from 0 answered to 96 and no test would have
noticed.

It now carries `assert_eq!(answered, 0)`, written by the dispatcher **before the
first lane was briefed**, so nobody can be said to have written their own
scorecard. Measured at the pin: **96 fuses, 0 answered, 96 refused, and all 96
give one reason** — *"a plane cuts this cone in a hyperbola"*. The family is
hyperbola-blocked outright, not partly, which prices the fuse work more sharply
than §46.2 could: what stands between this family and an answer is the drawing
lane, and the arrangement arms are behind it rather than beside it.

### 46.10 The spike, and what a fail re-scopes

Four explorations removed every structural risk the plan feared but one.
`what_a_run_between_these_two_lies_on` (`walk.rs:362-366`) is **already
run-keyed**; one pair yielding two differently-shaped runs is a working, tested
pattern (`intersect.rs:1836-1847` mints two runs differing only in `picked_by`,
and `walk.rs:1332-1348` filters by the run's ends and pickers and demands exactly
one survivor); and three of the four refused shapes need **no new geometry at
all**.

What no precedent covers is **endlessness**. A parabola arrives with
`nowhere_in_particular` ends both sides (`meet.rs:130-133`) and `walk` produces
points *between* the ends — of which there are none. `error.rs:343-346` already
raises this as the objection to fix (c).

So: a **20-minute spike**, its rule written before it runs. Target a right-angled
cone and a plane with normal `(0,1,1)` — the `E = 0` case
`the_seven_shapes_a_plane_cuts_a_cone_in.rs:1-29` says is reached exactly.
**Pass:** `walk` returns at least two points from a run with
`nowhere_in_particular` ends, every point on both surfaces within the published
roundoff. **Fail:** twenty minutes gone without that. *"It looks tractable"* is a
fail. *"The representation works but the range is open"* is a fail.

On fail the drawing lane drops to naming-only, the sentence loses its drawing
clause for parabola and hyperbola and keeps it for the two straight shapes, and
the recorded finding is that **endlessness, not conic classification, is what the
record has been mis-pricing since §43.6**. The spike runs beside the first wave,
which is dispatched without the lanes that depend on it: the spike can re-scope a
lane, not the unit.

### 46.11 The budget, in agent-hours, with the gate's share reserved first

§46.4 said the gate's budget is reserved before the first lane starts. Here is
the number: **9 agent-hours total, of which the gate takes 1.5, reserved first.**
The spike takes 0.35. What is left buys lanes at ~0.75 each.

If wave 2 runs short, the drop order is **the fuse lane > the quarter arc > the
two half-circles**: the fuse lane is the headline, the quarter arc pairs with the
front-door lane's `--ignored` fix, and the half-circles lane changes no published
sentence. Every lane commits at its halfway point whether or not its deliverable
is done, and every report carries a *what is left* section, empty if it finished
— lanes died mid-work last unit and their work died with them.

### 46.12 Three findings this unit hands the gate rather than fixing

Named here so the gate does not have to rediscover them, and so they are on a
list if the unit runs out of budget.

1. **The compiler forces zero edits when the run vocabulary grows.** `EdgeRun`
   and `SurfaceMeet` are `#[non_exhaustive]` in `rcad-geom` (`meet.rs:28-55`,
   `:171-173`), so every `match` on them in `rcad-topo` carries a wildcard and can
   never be exhaustive. `a_sixth_kind_of_surface.rs:9-18` already records this for
   `Surface`; nothing records it for runs, and a new run reads as *not straight*
   and *not closed* in a dozen places without a compiler error.
2. **22 production `panic!`/`unreachable!` in the fuse have gone uncounted for
   three units**, alongside the 30 `expect`s that have been counted.
3. **`TwoLinesThroughAConesApexAreOneCurveThroughItself` asserts a curve the
   kernel does not have to build.** Two straight runs told apart by pickers is
   enough, and `two_lines_told_apart` (`intersect.rs:1578-1608`) already does
   exactly that for another pair. The name argues for a representation the fix
   does not need.

### 46.13 The decision rule was written twice and the two forms disagree

§46.6 says the bucket **"shrinks by more than half"**. The unit's own plan, in
the dispatcher's notes, says **"≥ 50%"**. Nobody noticed until a lane came back
with a number that lands exactly between them: the KiCad bucket goes **168 → 84**,
which is 50.0% — over the line by one reading and short of it by the other.

**§46.6's text wins**, and the reason is written here rather than discovered
later: it is the form that is committed to the repository, and it is the
*stricter* of the two, so choosing it is choosing against the branch that
flatters the unit. A rule read after the number is a rule that was not a rule.

This is not the score. The gate generates the table at the final tree, over
**both** corpora and against the denominator §46.6 names — files that reach
`SolidBuilder::build`, now counted and printed by the lane as
`reached_the_solid_builder`. What is fixed here is only which side of the line
50.0% falls on if the final number lands there again.

**And a lane's number is not the unit's.** A later lane in this same unit fixes
the mesher bound that makes a hand-built fixture start importing, which moves
these rates — §45.7's failure mode, which is why no lane in this unit publishes
a rate and the gate publishes all of them.

## 47. The six arms, closed — recorded 2026-09-04

Ran 2026-09-03 19:37 to 2026-09-04 00:01, 4.4 hours of wall clock, 61 commits,
46 files, +7630/−640. **Twenty agents, about 6.2 agent-hours**, against a budget
of 9 with 1.5 reserved for the gate before the first lane started. The suite goes
from 1467 tests to **1508, none skipped** — the repo has no `#[ignore]` left for
the first time.

### 47.1 What it earned, and what it did not

**Earned, and falsifiable by counting:**

> **`where_a_plane_and_a_cone_cross` answers all six of its arms, and the kernel
> can draw every shape a plane cuts a cone in.**

Open `intersect.rs`, find the match on `(apex_is_on_the_plane, leaning)`, count
the arms that return `Err`: **zero**. Four variants were deleted outright and are
referenced nowhere in `crates/`. The parabola and each branch of the hyperbola
are walked into points on both surfaces; the ruling and the two lines through the
apex are straight runs told apart by pickers.

**Not earned: the fuse clause.** §46.1 said *and a frustum can be cut by a block*
would be added only if the fuse lane landed, and only against the pinned
assertion rather than a printed number. The fuse lane landed. The pin broke, 0
answered → 6 of 96. **And the clause is still false**, which is §47.2.

### 47.2 The pin was right and it was not enough

`AFrustumAgainstABlock` was pinned at `assert_eq!(answered, 0)` before any lane
was briefed, precisely so an improvement had to break a test rather than move a
`println!`. It broke, and the dispatcher re-derived the row at 6 answered and
wrote beside it: *"a block can now take a piece out of a frustum."*

**That sentence was false, and a lane sent to check it found out why.** The six
that answer are **all one row of the sixteen — the row where the block misses the
frustum altogether.** The block is always put down with its low corner at `x = 1`
and the frustum is never wider than `slope · far`, so the two are disjoint exactly
when `slope · far < 1`, and one row of the grid lands there. All six of its fuses
answer; all ninety fuses of the other fifteen rows refuse. **No block in that
family has ever cut a frustum.**

So the lesson is not "pin your numbers", which the unit already did. It is:

> **An assertion on a count is still a count.** A number moving in the right
> direction is not evidence that the thing the number stands for happened. What
> was missing was not a tighter pin — it was a check on what the answers *are*.

That check now exists: `Model::validate` on all six, volumes against closed forms
with the bound checked finite first, inclusion–exclusion across union and
intersection, both ways round, and a 40,625-point classification grid each answer
must match. All six pass it. They are right — they are just right about a case
nobody wanted to claim.

**And the ninety refusals moved, which is the real result.** They no longer say
*"a plane cuts this cone in a hyperbola"* — the geometry — but *"nothing can put
points in order along this curve"* — the arrangement. Demonstrated rather than
read off a label: `intersect` names the crossing, `where_a_closed_crossing_starts`
refuses both runs as `TheCrossingOfTheseTwoSurfacesIsNotClosed`, and the fuse
refuses after that. A hyperbola branch is a conic and is not closed, and *"round a
closed curve"* is the only conic order `arrange` has. **That is the next unit's
sentence, and this unit found it by moving a number and then asking what the
number meant.**

### 47.3 The first-refusal rule scores on its second branch

§46.6's rule, committed before the number was read, with the denominator named:
files that reach `SolidBuilder::build` — **265 of 323 KiCad, 11 of 44 NIST**.

The lane that stopped `brep.rs` overwriting the builder's own refusal measured
the curved-corner bucket at 168 → 84 on KiCad. **Two gates re-derived it at the
final tree and got 41% and 43.5% by independent routes** — because two later
lanes in the same unit moved it back up. So:

- the bucket does **not** shrink by more than half → **§46.6's second branch
  fires**, §45.3's relabelling is scored as noise, and option D's trigger is
  scored on the published number;
- **§46.13's tie-break is moot.** The unit spent a commit deciding which way 50.0%
  falls, and 50.0% was never the number. It is kept in the record because a rule
  read after the number is not a rule, and the discipline was right even though
  the boundary was irrelevant;
- no file-count projection is published, and the 68 B-spline files are not priced.

**§45.7 and §45.8 both score as right.** §45.8 predicted a lane's number would be
true when taken and false when merged, and that this is how the unit would lose.
It did happen, twice, and it cost nothing — because the plan forbade the lane
that measured it from publishing it, and made the gate generate it at the final
tree instead. **The prediction was correct and the countermeasure worked.**

What the corrected reporting bought, at the final tree: the 84 KiCad files that
stopped being called a corner name what actually stopped them — 44 crossings
where two surfaces are too nearly parallel to follow, 15 faces walking a closed
edge against the way its surface winds, 12 outer wires winding against the face
normal, 8 needing a half-space `f64` cannot write down. §43.5 and §44.6 cite 158
and 8 for these rows and are stale; the numbers above replace them.

### 47.4 Five published sentences were false, and two gates found them

The unit ran two closing gates in parallel — one re-deriving every load-bearing
number from the final tree, one auditing the claims. Between them, **five
sentences published in this repository were false at the tree that published
them**, none of which any lane caught:

1. **A volume "checked against the kernel's own published bound"** where the bound
   is `f64::INFINITY` for a pointed cone, because the radius of curvature goes to
   zero at the apex. `assert!(x <= inf)` cannot fail. The tree already forbade this
   exact pattern, in a file whose doc says to check against *a stated share of the
   deflection* rather than *dressing an unpublished number as a bound* — so the
   rule was written down and broken three hundred lines away.
2. **A winding rule justified by a case its own walker cannot produce.** The
   arithmetic was right (1.000 against 1.273); the pair is unreachable, because a
   bigger radius never gets fewer steps at one deflection. Confirmed twice, by
   different routes, 84,672 pairs and 24 × 64 pairs, zero sign flips.
3. **"This never refuses"**, five lines below the `# Errors` section documenting
   the two ways it refuses.
4. **"The length rule is the only thing that asks"** and **"every other check
   still runs over it"** — both measured by running one check in isolation and
   reporting its `Ok(())` as the fate of the model.
5. **"Reads as not straight, which is the safe side"** — where `false` is the
   two-arc branch, and two arcs where a ruling has one is a wrong answer, not a
   conservative one.

**Three of the five are one mistake**: a verdict measured on one function's return
value and reported as what the kernel does. That is now the standard those docs
are held to, written into them.

**And the number gate corrected two of its own verdicts an hour after publishing
them**, for the same reason: it had checked the number and stopped short of
checking the sentence the number was offered as evidence for. Recorded because it
is the cheapest available demonstration that the failure is structural and not a
lane being careless.

### 47.5 The unit's real yield was correctness, not the headline

The headline was a naming-and-drawing gap and it closed on schedule. What the
unit is actually worth is five holes nobody planned to find, four of them found
by asking a lane to justify a sentence it had already written.

| what | was |
|---|---|
| the winding of a flat face | certified **backwards** on a sliver — the walk comes back with zero points at pass 27, the margin collapses, and the corner polygon's sign is taken. Reachable under a tolerant policy, which is what the STEP door uses |
| a fuse of solids carrying a run the kernel cannot read | **committed an answer** — `Ok(fused)` built out of solids nothing can describe |
| a crossing shape with no row in the fuse | **crashed** the fuse, or was **skipped in silence** so a solid came back sound that nobody had looked at |
| a plane against a cone running straight | put **two arcs where a ruling has one** — the whole cone row, for three units |
| a model read back from bytes | took a face in no shell, a wire on no face, a coedge in no wire |

Each is now a refusal with a name, and each has a test. Four of the five are the
same shape: `EdgeRun` and `SurfaceMeet` are `#[non_exhaustive]` in `rcad-geom`, so
a new crossing kind arrives in `rcad-topo` **with zero compiler errors**, and this
is the unit that grew the vocabulary. Twenty-odd sites were swept and given
written verdicts; whether an edge closes now lives in **one** list rather than
six copies.

Two claims were re-classified in the direction §16.10 warns about. A hyperbola
whose apex plane does not round exactly was refused as a **limit**; the answer
existed — round the offset up, and check the near branch's clearance, which the
interval machinery already bounds from below — so it was a **gap**, and it is
closed. §43.6's row for two lines through a cone's apex argued no half-space can
pick one of two lines that cross; both halves true, conclusion false, and the
answer was one file away.

### 47.6 What was learned about running the work

- **Every lane committed at its halfway point and reported what was left.** No
  lane died holding work, which is what happened last unit.
- **Ownership was per file and it held.** Three lanes stopped at a file they did
  not own and reported instead of editing; one of them was right to, and the file
  it stopped at needed a change the dispatcher then made. One lane necessarily
  edited outside its list — a public signature change breaks its callers — and
  listed every file it touched and why.
- **Two lanes improved on their briefs and said so.** One was told to copy a rule
  into a second door and instead made both doors read one list, because *"the two
  had already drifted, which is the whole defect"*. One was told a defect existed
  in `rcad-geom/src/error.rs` — the dispatcher had the wrong crate — and fixed the
  right file rather than the named one.
- **The brief that produced the best work was the one that said what would count
  as failing.** The spike's rule was written before it ran and said in as many
  words that *"it looks tractable"* is a fail. It passed in five minutes.
- **A lane told to justify a sentence found the sentence wrong more often than a
  lane told to check code found a bug.** Four of the five false claims came from
  the claim gate, not the number gate.

### 47.7 What stands, and what the next unit picks up

**The named next thing**, and it comes with a demonstration rather than a guess:
*"nothing can put points in order along this curve"*, ninety times. Ordering
points along an endless bend is the whole of what stands between a cone and a
block now.

| open | where |
|---|---|
| **ordering along an endless bend** | the ninety refusals above. The next unit |
| **cones are absent from `fuses_that_must_agree.rs`** | commutativity, associativity, idempotence and absorption have **never** run over a cone |
| **the hyperbola's rounding chain is not derived** | the published `64·ε` rests on a 98-rounding **parabola** term count, and every measured worst case is a hyperbola |
| **a flat solid with a two-step face of no area** | passes `SolidBuilder::build` *and* `Model::validate`. Pinned by a test that asserts the gap |
| **two more copies of the closes-on-one-edge list** | `model.rs:591`, `builder.rs:366`. They fail safe today, so drift and not a hole |
| **`a_pair_that_crosses_in_a_conic` is a proxy for "closed conic"** | true for a hyperbola, which is not closed; the refusal arrives late instead of at the table |
| **the fuse drops the seam of a curved wall it never touched** | so `A ∪ B` for disjoint `A`, `B` does not hand `A` back at the topology level. Not new and not cone-specific — a round bar has done it since M2 |
| **the writer** | §46.8 item 3, unchanged. A ball that imports cannot be written out |
| **a tangent plane's single ruling** | still refused: `∇S × ∇Q` is exactly nothing where a plane rests on a cone's own side. The same limit as a plane on a pipe, one more surface pair |

### 47.8 The prediction

§45.8 predicted this unit would lose to a lane's number going stale. It did not,
because the plan forbade the measuring lane from publishing and made the gate
re-derive. **So the prediction for the next unit is about the thing that did get
through:** the six answered fuses were counted, asserted, re-derived and glossed
in a commit message — and the gloss was still false, because nobody looked at
*which* six until a lane was sent to. The next unit will publish a number that is
correct and a sentence about it that is not, and the countermeasure is the one
this unit found by accident: **for every rate that moves, name the cases that
moved and say what they have in common.**

## 48. Nothing round was ever checked — the unit after the six arms, recorded 2026-09-04

*Written before any lane was dispatched. Every file and line it cites was checked
against the tree at `0febd16`, by opening the file and not by trusting the report
that named it — two of the citations below changed when that was done, and one
correction was withdrawn outright. The corrections come first, for §46's reason:
a lane that reads a stale price scopes itself wrong on its first day.*

### 48.1 The name, and what the unit is

Called **nothing round was ever checked**, after the gap and not after the fix.
§46.7's rename is the precedent, and the reason to name a unit for its gap rather
than its hope is that a name stating a gap cannot be quietly satisfied by a lane
that widens one fixture list.

**`the cut` stays held.** §46.7 shelved it once for the unit where the conic
drawing landed; the drawing landed and the cut did not. It is shelved a second
time here. A name that has never been earned should not be spent early.

The unit's spine moved during planning, and it is worth saying why. It began as
the ordering work §47.7 names — *"nothing can put points in order along this
curve"*, ninety times — and that is still the kernel's missing capability. What
displaced it was reading what the fuse's own oracle actually covers.

### 48.2 Five corrections, before any lane reads them

**1. §47.7's *"cones are absent from `fuses_that_must_agree.rs`"* is understated,
and the accurate sentence is much worse.** Every property in that file that
compares invariants — inclusion–exclusion, idempotence, absorption,
associativity, the multi-argument rows and the difference identities — calls
`invariants_of` or `volume_of` at lines 367 through 840. Every use of the one
curved fixture is at lines 1128, 1183, 1222, 1275 and 1316. **The two sets do not
overlap at all.** The curved family runs **commutativity and nothing else**,
plus a pin on today's refusal and a disjoint case that answers nothing.

Transform invariance is worse than absent: `Answer::moved_by` **panics** on a
curved face (`fuses_that_must_agree.rs:2156-2159`), unconditionally on kind, so
even a pure translation of a ball would panic. Its own doc says the whole of the
obstacle — *"nothing here has worked out what it is on a pipe's axis."*

So roadmap §11.2's instruction — *"**Start with transform invariance.** Kernels
overfit badly to axis-aligned and origin-centred configurations"* — has never
once been carried out on a round face. Not on a cone. On a **cylinder**, which
has been in this kernel since M2.

This row has now been written down three times, each smaller than the truth:
*"cones are absent"*, then *"cones and spheres are absent"*, then the sentence
above. Each correction came from looking one level deeper at a row somebody had
already noticed and moved on from. That is §48.9's prediction.

**2. §46.4's named finding fired, and it is in the tree but not in this file.**
§46.4 said that if closing the hyperbola did *not* break `refused > 0` on the
corner-up-cube families, *"that is the finding — the hyperbola was not what
refused them."* It did not break, and
`how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs:600-618` records the whole thing: a
frustum answers 9 of 96 with 27 `AWireWillNotLieFlatOnItsFace` and 60 undecided,
a round bar of the same size in the same place answers **9 of 96 too** with 21
and 66, and therefore *"what those 87 refusals measure is a hard family, not a
hard surface."*

**The correction is to the correction.** This section first said the finding was
never recorded. It was — in the test file that measured it. What is true is
narrower: §47 does not carry it, so `decisions.md` alone does not tell a reader
that a cone is no worse than a cylinder on that family. Recorded this way because
the first draft of a corrections section getting a correction wrong is exactly
what §46.8 item 1 was, and the cheapest demonstration that reading the file
beats reading the report about the file.

**3. §47.3 promised to score option D's trigger and did not.** §44.6 states the
trigger so it can fire: *D fires when, after the named gaps close, more than half
the still-refused files are refused for a miss larger than `f64` rounding*,
scored there at 50% to 56% — on its own boundary. §47.3 says the trigger *"is
scored on the published number"* and then publishes the number without the
verdict. A fallback whose condition is never evaluated is a fallback with no
condition, which is the thing §44.6 was written to stop. **The closing gate
scores it.**

**4. `ACrossingThisCannotBeOrderedAlong` is two unrelated problems under one
name.** Its doc (`rcad-topo/src/error.rs:563`) cites ball × pipe and pipe × pipe
— a quartic nothing can order. The ninety frustum refusals are an open **conic**,
which is a different problem with a different fix. Any unit that moves either
count reports a number that mixes them.

**5. The laws suite cannot see an asymmetric non-manifold answer.**
`Err(Error::ResultIsNotManifold { .. })` returns `Ok(None)`
(`fuses_that_must_agree.rs:1572-1575`) on **every** family, including the ones
where an `Undecidable` refusal is a hard failure. So `A ∪ B` coming back
non-manifold while `B ∪ A` answers is silently skipped. That is
order-dependence, invisible to the suite whose job is finding it.

**What is not wrong, and was checked.** The vacuity guard is sound:
`SOME_COMPARISONS_MUST_HAPPEN = 0.3` (`:274`) with a `meant_to > 0` guard, so it
is not §47.4 item 1's shape. The file's own doc says the risk out loud at
`:9-13` — *"a green run says nothing on its own."* And the suite already picks
correctly between the bit-exact fingerprint and the invariant comparison per
property, which is better than roadmap §11.2 warns about.

### 48.3 The sentence the unit earns

> **Every algebraic law in `fuses_that_must_agree.rs` runs over a round solid,
> and transform invariance runs over one first.**

Falsifiable by counting: open the file, list the properties, and check each
one's fixtures for a curved entry. The second clause is roadmap §11.2's
instruction, followed four milestones late.

### 48.4 Wave one, and what each lane may write

| lane | one deliverable | may write |
|---|---|---|
| **L1 the fingerprint** | curved `moved_by`; the non-manifold asymmetry arm; wire curved fixtures into the properties that have never run over one | `tests/fuses_that_must_agree.rs` |
| **L2 the fixtures** | a ball and a frustum, with strategies, to signatures fixed before dispatch | `tests/pairs/mod.rs` |
| **L3 the claim audit** | claims of §16.10's shape in the two fuse files; the tangent-ruling pair is the seed | `src/fuse/arrange.rs`, `src/fuse/assemble.rs` |
| **L4 the seam question** | does a disjoint curved union validate, measure and classify right, and hand back a face with no seam? The **question**, not the fix | one new test file |
| **S the spike** | whether an open bend has a monotone key | scratchpad only |

**The ball comes before the cone.** A cone mostly refuses, so it buys vacuous
passes; `add_ball` is a public one-liner (`build.rs:719`) and a sphere has been
fuseable since M4. *"The laws have never run over a sphere"* is the more
embarrassing sentence and the cheaper one to fix.

**L1 and L2 are coupled by an interface, so the dispatcher fixes the fixture
signatures before either starts.** A lane inventing an interface the other lane
must guess is how two lanes become one.

**L4 takes the question and not the fix** because roadmap §11.2 says topological
equality is the wrong predicate — two correct kernels partition faces
differently. §47.7's dropped seam is a defect only if the answer validates while
carrying a face nothing cuts open, which is what
`ACurvedFaceGoesRightRoundWithNoSeam` exists to refuse. **That answer decides
whether the seam is this unit's top priority or a decomposition note**, and
guessing which would be picking the branch that suits the plan.

**Two rules whose pass and fail are written before the lane runs**, because §47.6
records that the brief which produced the best work was the one that said what
counted as failing:

- **L1's fingerprint stays bit for bit, or says why not.** A quarter turn about
  `z` is a swap and a negation (`pairs/mod.rs:259-279`), exact on a ball's
  centre, a pipe's axis and a cone's apex, and `Surface::transformed`
  (`rcad-geom/src/surface.rs:275`) already carries every scalar over untouched.
  **Pass:** the curved families pass `moving_a_pair_leaves_the_answer_alone` with
  no tolerance introduced anywhere. **Fail:** any bit difference — and on fail
  the lane names *which coordinate differed and why*, and drops that family to
  the invariant comparison while calling that a weakening in the doc rather than
  doing it quietly. The suite's one distinguishing property is that it has no
  tolerance in it; that is not traded for an afternoon.
- **The spike's rule.** The proposed key is `sign((p₁ − p₂) · (n × out))`, which
  drops a hyperbola's `cosh` term only if `out · (n × out)` is exactly zero. It
  is zero as a polynomial and merely near zero in `f64`, so the contamination is
  bounded by the walk's own `cosh σ ≤ 2` cap and the interval machinery reports
  `Undecidable` rather than lying. **Pass:** every sampled pair on one branch
  decides under a certified policy, and the order agrees with the parameter
  order, with zero disagreements. **Fail:** one undecided pair on a
  well-separated configuration, one disagreement, or thirty minutes gone.
  *"The contamination looks small"* is a fail.

### 48.5 The budget, with the gates reserved first

**9 agent-hours, of which two gates take 2.0, reserved before the first lane
starts.** The spike takes 0.35; what is left buys lanes at about 0.75. Wave one
is about 5.35 and wave two is composed from what wave one reports, not planned
here.

Two gates and not one, deliberately rather than by discovery: §47.4's two gates
between them found five false published sentences that twenty lanes missed, and
§47.6 records that **a lane told to justify a sentence found the sentence wrong
more often than a lane told to check code found a bug.** That is the best-value
time in the last unit and it is not the part that gets squeezed.

**Drop order: the spike, then the claim audit, then the seam question. L1 and L2
never drop, and never drop separately.** The spike goes first despite being the
cheapest thing here, because it is the only item whose result changes nothing in
*this* unit — it is pure input to the next one, and when hours are short the
thing to cut is the value that is entirely deferred.

**L1 as scoped is three deliverables and CLAUDE.md caps a lane at one.** It will
probably split. Its brief carries the commit-at-halfway rule and a *what is left*
section either way, per §47.6.

### 48.6 Two decisions that were made twice and disagreed

Written here rather than discovered later, which is §46.13's lesson applied
before the fact instead of after it.

- **The error-name split is not in this unit.** It was first settled as *"split
  it regardless of the spike"* and later as *"it pairs with the ordering lane."*
  The later form wins and the lane list has no slot for it: if no count moves
  this unit, splitting the name that reports the count is not yet urgent. It
  goes forward with the ordering lane.
- **The third way a crossing can run is decided and not built.** `HowItRuns`
  (`fuse/arrange.rs:448-467`) has two variants — a coordinate sort for endless
  straight runs and a cyclic order for closed curves — and an endless *curved*
  run has no representation at all. The decision, recorded now and built next
  unit, is to **add a third variant and leave `AlongAnAxis` alone**: its axis is
  chosen by `dominant_axis_of_a_direction`, which refuses when no coordinate has
  a provably nonzero component, and that guard is what catches a plane resting
  along a pipe's own side. Generalising it would put working, certified,
  guarded arithmetic behind new arithmetic to serve a case that does not need
  it.

| out | why |

| **the ordering lane** | the spike runs; the lane does not. It wants `arrange.rs`, which the claim audit is reading, and it is not this unit's spine |
| **cone against pipe** | roadmap §13 row 1, and it is what blocks `AFrustumAgainstABar` and `TwoFrustumsOnOneAxis`, both pinned at nothing answered. **This is the next unit's headline** |
