### 48.8 Two rules this unit adopts, and one of them is permanent

**Into §15, as a standing rule every later unit inherits:** *for every rate that
moves, name the cases that moved and say what they have in common.* §47.8 found
it by accident and §45.7, §46.9 and §47.2 are three consecutive units whose
central lesson was the same gap between a measurement and the claim it was
offered as evidence for. Three in a row is structural, and the per-unit form has
now been tried three times. **The closing gate may not accept a moved number
without its case list.**

**And this unit's own:** an open-table row must say what it **measured**, not
what it **noticed**. *"Cones are absent"* is noticed. *"Every property comparing
invariants runs at lines 367 to 840 and every curved fixture at 1128 to 1316,
and the sets do not overlap"* is measured. §48.2 item 1 is what the difference
costs.

**The corrections section is audited like anything else.** §46.8 item 1 was a
mis-priced correction sitting inside the section named for corrections, and
§48.2 item 2 is one this unit caught on itself before publishing. The closing
claim gate reads §48.2 with the same suspicion it reads a doc comment.

### 48.9 The prediction

§47.8 predicted a correct number with a false sentence attached, and Q3's rule
above is the countermeasure. **The prediction for the unit after this one is
about what this planning session actually demonstrated:** it loses to a row in an
open table that is *true but too small*. §47.7's cone row was written down three
times, each time accurately and each time smaller than the fact, and every
correction came from asking what the row had been measured against rather than
reading it again.

So: **the next unit's largest finding is already written in §47.7 or §48.7, in a
row nobody has priced.** The countermeasure is §48.8's second rule, and the way
to score this prediction is to check, at the next gate, whether the unit's
biggest surprise had a row waiting for it.

### 48.10 The spike passed, and the risk it was written for does not exist

*Added after the spike ran. §48.4 is left exactly as it was written — rewriting a
pass rule to match a pass is the discipline this unit is named for.*

**PASS**, against §48.4's rule and with no part of it relaxed.

| curve | ordered pairs asked | undecided | out of order |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| parabola | 4 920 | 0 | 0 |
| one branch of a hyperbola | 11 480 | 0 | 0 |

All under `Policy::certified()`, all settled by intervals, with the exact level
never reached. Fixtures span cones of slope 0.25, 1 and 4, and planes through
the origin and 500 units out.

The key is what §48.4 proposed:

> `sign((ahead − behind) · (n × the_bend's_own_way))`

where `the_bend's_own_way` is a parabola's `bend` or a hyperbola branch's `out`,
and `n` is the cutting plane's stored normal.

**The contamination §48.4 budgeted for is not small — it is absent, and the
reason is a spelling.** §48.4 wrote that `own_way · (n × own_way)` is *"zero as a
polynomial and merely near zero in `f64`"*, and reasoned that the walk's
`cosh σ ≤ 2` cap bounds what that costs. That reasoning applies only if the cross
product is built as three `f64`s first. **Kept inside `Exact` as a determinant,
the triple product returns `Decision::Zero`, asserted, on every fixture.** It is
the choice `HowThreeOnACurveWind` already makes about not building its fourth
point, one level further down.

The built-vector spelling would also have passed — the worst own-way term
measured is `4.65e-17` against a signal of `9.95` — but that is luck and not a
cancellation, and the determinant is what the ordering lane should write.

**The check has teeth, which is the number that makes the zeroes worth reading.**
Aimed down `across` instead — a direction the quadratic term does *not* cancel
against — the identical tally reports **404 out of order and 13 undecided out of
820**. Resolution, found by halving the gap until it refuses, is about `1e-16`
relative on both curves: the `f64` grid itself, not a margin the triple product
eats into.

**What it does not show, stated because §48.8's rule cuts both ways.** Every
sample is an exact point; `arrange.rs` passes boxes at three-surface corners, and
nothing here says a wide box decides — though every pair settled at level 2 with
the exact level unused beneath it. And only plane-against-cone was tried, because
it is the only pair that makes an open bend today; `n` being a *plane's* normal is
part of the key, so an open bend from a pair with no plane in it needs its own
derivation.

**So the ordering work is priced, and it is not roadmap §13 row 1.** What stands
between a block and a frustum is one `HowItRuns` variant (§48.6), one predicate
that now exists in production shape, and the call sites. The predicate is kept on
the branch `worktree-agent-a1820cae9666ed345` rather than thrown away with the
worktree.

## 49. Nothing round was ever checked, closed — recorded 2026-09-04

56 commits, 22 files, +7352/−344. **Thirteen lanes, one spike and two closing
gates**, against a budget of 9 agent-hours with 2.0 reserved for the gates before
the first lane started. The suite goes from **1508 to 1579 tests, none skipped**.

### 49.1 The sentence was not earned, and the gate is why we know

§48.3 said:

> Every algebraic law in `fuses_that_must_agree.rs` runs over a round solid, and
> transform invariance runs over one first.

**The first clause is false at the closing tree.** The number gate listed the
properties and their fixtures rather than reading the doc:

| | laws |
|---|---|
| **run and compare** over a round solid | 4 — commutativity (bar, ball, frustum), inclusion–exclusion (ball), idempotence and `A \ A = ∅` (ball, bar), transform invariance (bar, ball) |
| **have a round fixture and compare nothing**, pinned at a refusal | 4 — absorption, `A \ (A \ B) = A ∩ B`, `((A ∪ B) \ B) ∪ B`, associativity over the trio |
| **have no round fixture at all** | 3 — the two multi-argument chains and the repeated-union property |

Curved fixture sites went **5 → 19** and laws comparing over a round solid
**1 → 4**. That is a large move and it is not *every*.

**The second clause is true and fully earned.** Transform invariance runs over a
round solid bit for bit with no tolerance introduced; `moved_by` handles all five
surface kinds and the panic that stood in its way is gone. Its one weakening — the
round rows shift and never turn — was checked against the public API by the gate
and is a **limit**: `Isometry` has exactly one turn-bearing constructor, and
`cos(π/2)` in `f64` is not zero.

**The honest sentence, and it is the one this unit earned:**

> **Four of the eleven algebraic laws now run over a round solid where one did,
> transform invariance is the first of them, and the seven that do not are each
> pinned at a named refusal rather than passing green.**

### 49.2 The unit's largest result is a wrong answer it introduced and caught

**A fuse ordered a closed quartic loop as an endless straight line.** Two
cylinders whose stored axis directions are *not* parallel — exact cross
`5.1e-17` — but whose `f64` cross rounds to exactly zero, because both products
round to `0x1.7271392ba6f36p-2`. The straight gate said parallel, `intersect`
said `RightRoundWhereItsFacesCross`, and `how_a_crossing_runs` returned
`AlongAnAxis`.

Yesterday that pair **refused**. A lane closing a real gap — two overlapping
parallel pipes were refusing for no arithmetic reason, because the two doors
disagreed — carried a rounded test into a place where it decides an answer
instead of a refusal. **The trade this kernel exists not to make, made by a lane
fixing something else, and reachable from file data** (`rcad-step`'s reader
builds a `Cylinder` straight from the file).

The closing claim gate found it. Not a lane, not the number gate, and not the
dispatcher, who had verified the lane's own claims and merged it.

**And the fix found a bigger one underneath.** The plane-against-pipe row of the
same two doors had the identical defect and it is **older than this unit**: of
45 186 near-square planes drawn against random pipe axes, **9 239 — one in five —
have a stored normal whose `f64` dot with the axis is exactly zero and whose
exact dot is not**, and `intersect` names every one of those crossings a closed
ellipse. Each was being ordered along an axis. Both rows are now three-way
predicates — `Pos`, `Zero`, or `Undecidable` carrying its enclosure — asked by
both doors, in the style `along_a_crossing.rs` already uses.

**A third rounded row is still rounded.** `a_plane_cuts_a_cone_in_rulings`
decides a degree-six expression in plain `f64`, and its doc still claims that
disagreeing with `intersect` costs a refusal rather than a wrong answer. By the
two findings above that is likely false in the same way. **It is not
demonstrated**, and the lane that found the other two said so instead of
assuming. It wants its own lane.

> **§49.8 closes this: it was demonstrated, and it was a bug.** The paragraph
> above stands as written because it was right to refuse to claim it — but the
> claim it declined to make was true, and the row is now three of three.

### 49.3 What else the two gates found that thirteen lanes did not

**Option D fires.** §42.9's fallback has been carried for three units with its
condition never evaluated; §44.6 wrote the condition so it could fire and scored
it at 50–56%, "exactly on its own boundary"; §47.3 promised to score it and did
not; §48.2 item 3 sent it to this gate. Scored on §44.6's own denominator: 323
KiCad files, 226 refused, 73 accounted for by named gaps still open, leaving
**153 of which 94 miss by more than `f64` rounding — 61.4%**. Both corpora,
50.8%. It is clear of its boundary, and the numerator can only grow with better
instrumentation, so the verdict is one-sided safe.

**§48.9's prediction landed inside this unit's own tree.** The frustum family's
comparison floor is justified by *"eighteen fresh-seed runs came out between 30%
and 46% … a margin of ten points."* The gate ran 24 seeds and measured **25.4% to
52.4%**. The decision to lower the floor is *better* supported than its own
evidence — the old floor would have failed on the gate's first run — but the
sentence beside it is false and the margin is **5 points, not ten**. A number
that was right with a sentence about it that was not, which is exactly what
§47.8 predicted and §15.10 was written to catch.

**Seventeen published sentences were false or overstated**, against §47.4's five
in the unit before. Three deserve naming because of where they were:

1. `Measurement::volume_error` and `Measurement::area_error` — **public API
   contracts** — both promised the mesh never overestimates. A cube of side 8
   with a radius-1 hole measures **0.477 too much** at deflection 0.1; an 8×8
   plate half a unit thick with the same hole measures **0.127 too much** skin
   while the same hole eight deep measures 0.128 too little. The magnitude bound
   survives two-sided; the sign was the lie.
2. `ResultIsNotManifold { count: 1 }` was recorded as **withdrawn** in §38.6,
   repeated in §39.4, and told to every future lane by the `fuse-debugging`
   skill. It is **live**: 83 268 fuses reach it in two of six families, and its
   sharpest form has no curve and no rounding in it — three axis-aligned boxes on
   the integer grid where `fuse([far, near], [bar], Intersection)` refuses while
   `near ∩ bar` alone answers with volume 2 and validates. **The argument that
   contributes nothing turns an answer into a refusal.** The four families the
   old record was written from reach it in none of 3 000 fuses each, which is why
   it looked closed.
3. A lane corrected a sentence about cone crossings in `assemble.rs` and left the
   identical sentence standing in `arrange.rs`. **The tree now carries the
   corrected and uncorrected forms of one sentence, two files apart** — this
   unit's own recurring finding, happening to this unit.

**Two latent defects with named one-line fixes**, neither exercised today:
`settle_on_the_lower_rounding` never removes the superseded key, so a coordinate
no corner sits on can merge a later differently-named corner into an old one; and
`three_planes_faced_the_one_way` canonicalises to `-0.0` where its sibling adds
`+ 0.0` to avoid exactly that, and `total_cmp` sorts `-0.0 < 0.0`.

### 49.4 What was fixed, and what each cost to find

| what | was |
|---|---|
| a fuse depending on which way round its arguments were handed over | **on axis-aligned whole-number input** — §17.7's control family. Fixed in three lines: a solid's own planes now cut its own faces. Volume 10 and area 38 against hand arithmetic, not against the other order |
| one corner named twice | two solids flush on a plane hold it facing opposite ways, and `CornerName::Meet` keyed on the stored coefficients, so `P` and `−P` were two names. `name_of_the_surface_either_way_round` already existed and was wired into two of its three call sites |
| two parallel pipes refusing for no arithmetic reason | the two doors disagreed; one had a real test and the other swept the pair into a blanket `false` |
| one plane and two quadrics refusing on sight | where two quadrics share a quadratic form, their difference is **linear** — so the triple was two planes and a quadric all along, and needed no quartic |
| a fuse giving up over a triple that provably has no corner | `intersect` is now asked about the two partners, and only `SurfaceMeet::Nothing` skips. Pinned in both directions: never-skip fails 4 tests, always-skip fails exactly 2 |
| a mesh's measured volume with no published bound | `skin · d · (R/(R−d))²`, infinite unless `d < R`, worst ratio 0.1999 and loosest 0.00446, with the exponent fitted over 60 points: the error goes as `d¹`, and `d²` under-predicts the finest point by **124×** |

### 49.5 What was learned about running the work

- **The gates earned their reserved budget twice over.** They found the
  regression, Option D's verdict, §48.3's falsity and the frustum floor's false
  margin — none of which any of thirteen lanes reported, and one of which the
  dispatcher had already verified and merged.
- **§48.4's stated risk was a spelling, not a fact.** The spike was written to
  test whether a triple product that is zero as a polynomial is decidable in
  `f64`. Kept inside `Exact` as a determinant it is exactly `Decision::Zero`;
  built as three `f64`s first it is 4.65e-17 against a signal of 9.95 — which
  would also have passed, and is luck rather than cancellation. **The same
  distinction is the whole of §49.2.** The unit learned it in a 20-minute spike
  and then shipped a bug that is the same mistake in a different file.
- **A lane told to justify a sentence beat a lane told to check code, again.**
  Both gates ran on the same tree for a comparable budget; the claim gate found
  the wrong answer.
- **Two lanes improved on their briefs by contradicting them.** One was told a
  seamless cylinder wall is what `ACurvedFaceGoesRightRoundWithNoSeam` exists to
  refuse — it is not, that refusal is gated on a surface that *pinches*, and a
  cylinder does not. One was told to expect a frustum family at 9 of 96 and found
  two fifths of it answering, then found the rule that says which two fifths and
  pinned it at 84 of 84.
- **Three of thirteen lanes patched a `.rs` file with a heredoc or `sed -i`**,
  which CLAUDE.md bans categorically, and all three reported themselves. A rule
  broken by a fifth of the lanes that had read it is a rule the tooling does not
  enforce. Recorded rather than enforced, by decision.
- **A lane's brief that named what would count as failing produced better work
  than one that named what to build**, for the third unit running.

### 49.6 What stands

| open | where |
|---|---|
| ~~**the third rounded row**~~ | **closed by §49.8.** It was a bug, and it needed both of its two signs to be wrong at once |
| **ordering along an endless bend** | the spike passed: `sign((p₁ − p₂) · (n × own_way))`, 16 400 pairs, none undecided, none out of order. One `HowItRuns` variant and the call sites. **X2 measured what it buys**: the frustum family answers iff `slope · (roof − apex) < distance to the nearest side wall`, 84 of 84, so this is the other three fifths |
| **`CannotTellTheCellsOfAFaceApart`** | no longer undemonstrated. A face with a round hole has a rim wire of one closed edge, and a one-corner wire has no winding to read. Blocks associativity over a curved trio |
| **the general quartic** | plane and two quadrics that bend differently. The pencil route wants `det(λM₁ + μM₂) = 0`, whose cubic roots are not exact, so every sign below them is a box |
| **`ResultIsNotManifold` with `count` other than 1** | entirely unmeasured — 864 of 31 104 in an exhaustive pair sweep, counted by nothing |
| **`select` on a curved cap** | two overlapping parallel bars now get past geometry and stop here, undecided with an unbounded enclosure |
| **the two latent corner defects** | §49.3, both with one-line fixes named |
| **`cuts.rs` and most of `three_surfaces.rs`** | **unaudited**, and recorded as unaudited rather than as clean — the claim gate audited by targeted attack and said so |
| **the writer, the torus, cone against pipe** | unchanged from §47.7 |

### 49.7 The prediction

§48.9 predicted this unit would lose to a row in an open table that is *true but
too small*, and it did — the frustum floor's "30% to 46%" was measured over
eighteen runs and is 25.4% to 52.4% over twenty-four. The countermeasure held:
the gate caught it because §15.10 forbids accepting a moved number without its
case list.

**So the prediction for the next unit is about what got through instead.** The
regression in §49.2 was introduced by a lane whose every claim was true, verified
by a dispatcher who checked each of them, and caught only because a gate went
looking for sentences rather than numbers. Nothing in the number gate's ten rows
would have found it, because **the defect was not in any number anybody
published** — it was in an expression nobody had asked to be exact.

> **The next unit will ship a correct fix that carries a rounded test into a
> place where it decides an answer.** The countermeasure is the one §49.5 names:
> when a change moves a test from a place that refuses to a place that answers,
> the test itself has to be proved and not merely reused. Score it by asking, at
> the next gate, whether any predicate reached a new call site without being
> re-derived there.

### 49.8 The third row was a bug too, and three of three is a class

Run after §49 was written, on the row §49.6 listed first among what stands.

**The dangerous direction is the same one**: the gate says *straight*, the
crossing is really a conic, and `how_a_crossing_runs` returns `AlongAnAxis` —
**a closed ellipse ordered along an axis**, exactly as the cylinders were.

What hid it is that it takes **both** of the function's two signs being wrong at
once, which is why nobody found it by inspection:

| the gate said | the truth | draws | what happened |
|---|---|---:|---|
| rulings | one closed ellipse | **3 655** | `AlongAnAxis`, all 3 655. **Not one refused** |
| rulings | the apex alone | 16 077 | no run exists to order |
| a curve | two rulings | 7 761 | harmless **only** because `intersect` refuses to name a near-tangent ruling direction |

Out of 360 000 draws over three families. Either sign wrong alone is safe: a
rounded apex with `E < 0` makes the truth a hyperbola, and `intersect` refused
all **17 645** of those because a branch clearance of about `1e-17` cannot beat
one ulp of `n·a`; a rounded lean with the apex genuinely on the plane makes the
truth `TouchAtOnePoint`, and no run exists. Both wrong together names one closed
ellipse and calls it two rulings.

Both signs are now exact `Decision` predicates asked by both doors, with the lean
written as `(n·w)² − Σ(slope·(n_j w_k − n_k w_j))²` so it needs only squares of
short expansions and never a product of two long ones. The nearly-tangent plane
that used to be misordered is now **ordered correctly** — `RoundAClosedCurve` —
which is a better landing than the plane-and-pipe row got, because a cone's
ellipse is not `1/(n·w)` long and a place to start on it is still findable. Every
cone rate is bit-identical, including the frustum-against-a-block row at 90 of 96.

**The reuse was not achieved and that is the open item.** `intersect` computes
both signs exactly already, inside `where_a_plane_and_a_cone_cross`, over an
`Exact` that is `pub(crate)`. Asking one question in one place needs two
functions exported from `rcad-geom`, which was outside the lane's write set — so
the expression now exists in a third copy, guarded by a 360 000-draw test
asserting the door and `intersect` agree on every draw. **That guard is not the
same thing as not having a copy**, and §49.5's lesson says so.

> **Closed.** The copy is gone. Both signs are built once, in
> `intersect.rs`'s `where_the_apex_stands` and `how_the_plane_leans`, and asked
> two ways: `where_a_plane_and_a_cone_cross` puts them through the policy, and
> the two exported functions `where_a_cones_apex_stands_against_a_plane` and
> `how_a_plane_leans_against_a_cone` stop at the cascade, which is what both
> doors call. **The doors take no `Policy` on purpose** — a tolerant one may read
> an enclosure the cascade refused as nothing, and a `Zero` a door has not earned
> is what calls a closed ellipse two rulings. The two therefore part company only
> under a tolerant policy and only into a refusal, which is the trade
> `a_plane_lies_along_a_pipes_axis` already states one row down. The 360 000
> draws stay: with one implementation they no longer compare two spellings of the
> arithmetic, and what they check now is the *table* — this pair of signs means
> straight, that pair means curved — against the shape `intersect` names, which
> is still written out in both crates. Every rate is bit-identical, the frustum
> row included.

**Three rounded gates, three bugs, all the same shape**: an `f64` expression
compared against zero, believed to fail into a refusal, in fact failing into a
wrong answer. That is not three incidents. The next unit should ask what *else*
in `arrange.rs` and `assemble.rs` decides a shape by comparing a sum of products
to zero, and treat a rounded answer there as a defect until it is shown
otherwise — the reverse of the burden these three carried.

Two paths remain unexercised and are recorded as such rather than as clean: the
`None`/`Undecidable` arm of these predicates never fired in 360 000 draws or
anywhere in the suite, and neither did its twin next door; and the 7 761 draws of
the safe direction are safe only until
`TwoLinesThroughAConesApexAreOneCurveThroughItself`'s neighbouring gap closes.

## 50. The endless bend — the unit after nothing round was ever checked, recorded 2026-09-04

*Written before any lane was dispatched. Every file and line it cites was checked
against the tree at `4b3ecda` by opening the file, not by trusting the report that
named it. Three citations changed when that was done and one of them changed the
scope of a lane, which is §48's preamble earning its place a second time.*

### 50.1 The name, and what the unit is

Called **the endless bend**, after the thing the kernel cannot do: put points in
order along a curve that has no ends. §47.7 named it, §48.7 held it out with the
reason *"it wants `arrange.rs`, which the claim audit is reading"*, and §48.10's
spike then passed on it. It has been the missing capability for three units and
it is now the spine of one.

**`the cut` stays held**, a third time. It has still never been earned.

The unit is two things that turn out to be one. Ordering along an endless bend is
the capability; **cone against pipe** — §48.7's *"this is the next unit's
headline"* — is the consumer that proves it, because a cone and a pipe on one
axis cross in exactly the kind of curve that has no ends. Shipping the ordering
without the consumer would be a `HowItRuns` variant nothing constructs.

### 50.2 Five corrections, before any lane reads them

**1. §49.3 describes the second latent defect as something the function does not
do.** It says `three_planes_faced_the_one_way` *"canonicalises to `-0.0` where its
sibling adds `+ 0.0`"*. Opening `arrange.rs:396-411`: the function does not
canonicalise to anything. It calls `flat.reversed()` when the first nonzero
coefficient is negative, and reversing a plane whose *other* coefficients are
`0.0` is what **produces** `-0.0`. The sibling is `exactly_at`
(`assemble.rs:1882-1889`), which maps `-0.0 → 0.0` with a comment saying why, and
the key that tells the two apart is `in_the_order_a_float_compares`
(`arrange.rs:419-422`), a `total_cmp`-equivalent ordering.

The defect is real and §49.3 was right that it is one. But a lane briefed to
"stop it canonicalising to `-0.0`" would look for a canonicalisation that is not
there. The fix is on the *producing* side or the *ordering* side, and which one is
the lane's to decide.

**2. `HowItRuns` has moved.** §48.6 cites `fuse/arrange.rs:448-467`; it is now
`arrange.rs:495-513`, with the same two variants. Ordinary drift, recorded because
§48.6 is where the third variant was decided and it is the paragraph a lane will
be sent to read.

**3. The §49.8 directive was priced as a lane and it is not one.** *"What else in
`arrange.rs` and `assemble.rs` decides a shape by comparing a sum of products to
zero"* sounds like a sweep of two 3 000-line files. Counted: **20 sites in
production code** — 12 in `arrange.rs` (`:358, 408, 1264, 1306, 1337, 1864, 1949,
3529, 3648`, plus `:419`), 8 in `assemble.rs` (`:248, 1122, 1129, 1135, 1666,
1826, 1887`) — and most already go through `Interval::sign()` or return a
`Decision` rather than comparing floats. The raw `== 0.0` sites are `assemble.rs`
`:1887`, `:248` and `:1122`. **This is a gate charge, not a lane**, and it is
moved to §50.7 accordingly. It also collided head-on with the ordering lane, which
writes the same file; making it a gate charge dissolves the collision rather than
scheduling around it, and buys independence — an audit of new code by the lane
that wrote it is what §49.7 predicts will go wrong.

**4. Lane A's scope is bounded by an arm in another crate, and the arm says so
itself.** `assemble.rs:2118-2123` returns `false` — *this crossing holds no
straight line* — for a cone against a ball, a pipe or another cone, and its
comment states the whole hazard:

> ***`false` rests on `intersect` and not on the geometry*** *… two cones that
> share an apex meet along rulings, which are lines. No such pair reaches here …
> so this arm is right for as long as that refusal stands, and is the arm to
> revisit the day it lifts.*

This unit lifts part of that refusal. **Coaxial cone against pipe is safe**: they
cross in circles, which hold no lines, so `false` stays right. **Cone against cone
is not**, and naming it would turn that arm into a wrong answer of exactly
§49.8's shape — an arm believed safe because a refusal upstream holds, failing
into an answer rather than a refusal when the refusal lifts. So Lane A names the
coaxial cone-and-pipe case **and nothing else**, and the day cone-and-cone is
named, `assemble.rs:2118` is the first thing that changes.

**5. §50.10's prediction fired inside this section, before a single lane ran.**
Pruning the lane worktrees turned up two branches that were never merged and
that looked like stranded fixes, and this section was about to carry both into
the wave:

- `m5-predicates-scaling` — *"meet_of_three_planes retries scaled per plane on
  refusal"*, which is the case CLAUDE.md §16.10 cites by name: *"true of
  orderings and silent about scalings, and a representable answer was refused
  for it."* It is **already in main, byte for byte**.
  `git diff m5-predicates-scaling:crates/rcad-predicates/src/planes.rs
  main:crates/rcad-predicates/src/planes.rs` is empty. `meet_after_rescaling_each_plane`,
  `meet_of_three_planes_at_this_scale` and `rescaled` all stand at
  `planes.rs:48-160` with the branch's own doc wording. The fix reached main by
  another route and the branch's merge was never recorded, so `git
  merge-base --is-ancestor` still calls it unmerged and it reads, at a glance,
  like work somebody dropped.
- `rcad-fuzz` — **not** superseded, and not whole either. Main fixed the same
  overflow by a different route (`power_of_two_that_keeps_the_squares_in_range`,
  `point.rs:367`) rather than the branch's divide-by-the-largest-component, so
  the *fix* may be dead while the *tests* are not: the branch's
  `a_vector_too_huge_to_square_is_normalized_by_dividing_first` is in no file in
  main, and `crates/rcad-geom/tests/soak/mod.rs` does not exist in main at all.

**The prediction was that the next unit would build something the tree already
has, somewhere else. It took the planning session, not a lane.** The
countermeasure named there — grep before writing, not after review — is what
found it, one turn after the recommendation to carry both was made. An unmerged
branch is not evidence of unlanded work; it is evidence of an unrecorded merge,
and the two look identical from `git branch --no-merged`.

### 50.3 The sentence the unit earns

> **The fuse can put points in order along a curve that never ends, and a cone
> coaxial with a pipe is cut by it.**

Falsifiable two ways: `HowItRuns` has a third variant with a construction site
that is not a test, and `intersect.rs:181` no longer refuses the coaxial pair.

### 50.4 The shape of the wave, and what each lane may write

**Spike first, alone.** It is short, and it settles two things at once: whether
coaxial really is one sign question, and what the predicate's signature is. That
signature goes in this section before A, B and C start, because a lane inventing
an interface another lane must guess is how two lanes become one (§48.4).

| step | one deliverable | may write |
|---|---|---|
| **S the spike** | is coaxial cone-against-pipe one sign question? | scratchpad only, never merged |
| **E the oracles** | `rcad-fuzz`'s order and scale oracles, re-applied (§50.9) | `tests/fuzzing/mod.rs`, `tests/every_pair_of_surfaces_the_fuzzer_draws_is_named_honestly.rs`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/where_two_surfaces_cross.rs` |
| **F the soak** | a shared soak module, the `checked_mul` bug, the missing knife-edge arm (§50.9) | `tests/soak/mod.rs`, `tests/how_far_the_marcher_strays_from_a_crossing_that_is_a_circle.rs`, `tests/every_point_along_a_crossing_is_on_both_surfaces.rs`, `tests/the_same_pair_turned_names_the_same_kind_of_crossing.rs`, `tests/how_often_naming_a_crossing_refuses.rs`, `rcad-topo/tests/turning_a_fuse.rs` |
| **A the crossing** | name the coaxial pair; split `intersect.rs:181`'s arm | `rcad-geom`: `intersect.rs`, `error.rs`, `walk.rs`, its own tests |
| **B the bend** | third `HowItRuns` variant, the ordering call sites, and the 84 of 84 | `rcad-topo/src/fuse/arrange.rs` |
| **C the consumer** | `settle_on_the_lower_rounding`'s superseded key; split the two frustum families' pin apart, and re-word `assemble.rs:2118`'s comment to cite the circles rather than the refusal (§50.11) | `rcad-topo/src/fuse/assemble.rs`, `rcad-topo/tests/how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs` |
| **D the negative zero** | the second latent defect, which spans both files | `arrange.rs` **and** `assemble.rs`, after B and C merge |

**A, B and C run concurrently. D is serialized behind both.** D is one defect
owning two small regions in two files that other lanes are writing; splitting it
across B and C would put the failing test — which CLAUDE.md rule 2 requires
*first* — in a place where neither half can make it fail for the right reason.

**C is thin without the consumer.** `settle_on_the_lower_rounding` is one private
function with one caller (`assemble.rs:1774`). Giving C the `assemble.rs` side of
A's work is what stops A shipping a predicate with nothing calling it, which §13
says should not be built at all.

### 50.5 The five rules whose pass and fail are written before the lane runs

§47.6 and §49.5 both record that the brief which said what counted as *failing*
produced better work than the brief that said what to build. Three units running.

- **S.** **Pass:** every coaxial pair in the draw decides under a certified
  policy, zero undecided, at §48.10's bar of a comparable draw. **Fail:** one
  undecided pair on a well-separated configuration, or forty minutes gone. A
  non-zero count is **not** a unit failure — it is the spike working, and cone
  against pipe converts from code to a written answer under §50.6's rule.
- **A.** **Fail:** the coaxial case is named but `intersect.rs:181` still raises
  `ACrossingBetweenAConeAndAnotherCurvedSurface` for it; or the *"not named at
  all"* claim at `intersect.rs:110-114` is left standing; or anything beyond the
  coaxial pair is named (§50.2 item 4); or `error.rs:331-335`'s *"one sign
  question apiece"* is left standing, which §50.11 showed is wrong twice over —
  there is no shape question, and there are two coaxiality signs, not one. **Also
  a fail: reporting this work as moving the import rate.** It moves it by zero
  files and §50.11 measured that before the lane ran.
- **B.** **Fail:** the frustum family answers fewer than **84 of 84**; or any new
  call site of the ordering predicate carries the spike's derivation instead of
  its own. §49.6 published 84 of 84 on a spike's word and §15.6 says a published
  bound needs a test.
- **C.** **Fail:** the `assemble.rs:2121` refusal still fires for a coaxial pair
  that A now names.
- **D.** **Fail:** either latent-defect test passes against the unfixed code.

**At forty-five minutes a lane commits what is done, writes what is left, and
hands back** (CLAUDE.md). The handback point is named per lane so that "what is
left" is not "a tree that does not compile": for **B** the variant and its match
arms land first and the 84 of 84 is a second commit; for **A** the dispatch arm
splits first and the shape discriminant is second.

### 50.6 What stays out

| out | why |
|---|---|
| **cone against cone, cone against ball** | §50.2 item 4. Naming either makes `assemble.rs:2118` a wrong answer |
| **torus against anything curved** | six pairs unnamed; untouched by this unit |
| **`cuts.rs`, most of `three_surfaces.rs`** | §49.6 records them **unaudited**, and they stay recorded that way. §50.7 charge 5 covers two files, not four |
| **`ResultIsNotManifold` with `count` other than 1** | 864 of 31 104 and counted by nothing. Unmeasured is not this unit's spine |
| **the writer, fillets, B-splines** | unchanged. Fillets stay gated on §44.7's reason |
| **connecting `BSplineSurface`** | built, tested, and reachable from nothing. Left deliberately: §13 wants a named consumer and §14356 already sent the free-form marcher away. Recorded here so it is a decision and not an omission |

### 50.7 The gate's five charges

Named, because §49.5 found that briefs naming failure beat briefs naming work, and
a gate is a brief like any other.

1. **Re-derive 84 of 84** on the frustum family, independently of B's test.
2. **Score §49.7's prediction.** Name every call site the ordering predicate
   reached, and check each carries its own derivation and not the spike's.
3. **Run both latent-defect tests against the unfixed code** and confirm they
   fail. A test that passes without the fix proves nothing.
4. **Read the audit's negative claims for §16.10 shape.** An audit's output is
   mostly *"this one is fine"*, and a negative claim needs a demonstration and not
   a paragraph.
5. **The §49.8 sweep**, moved here from a lane by §50.2 item 3: the 20 sites, after
   A, B, C and D have landed, so that the sweep sees the new call sites. If the
   class is found present, say so about `cuts.rs` and `three_surfaces.rs` too —
   they become *more likely dirty than before*, not unchanged.

### 50.8 The machinery this unit changes before it dispatches

None of this is a deliverable. All of it is done before the spike runs, because
each one is cheap now and expensive during a wave.

- **Worktrees move out of the repo.** They are created at
  `.claude/worktrees/<name>` inside the tree; 38 of them held **166 GB**, and
  `.gitignore` did not cover them, so `git add -A` at the root would stage the
  lot. The cause is exact and not neglect: the harness sweep keeps any worktree
  with unpushed commits, **this repo has no remote**, so every lane branch was
  unpushed and the sweep kept all 38 for ever. They move to a sibling
  `rcad-worktrees/`, which is where the 14 hand-made ones already live.
  `.claude/worktrees/` is gitignored anyway, as insurance against the default
  coming back.
- **The repo gets a remote.** 67 000 lines of source and 51 000 of tests exist in
  one place on one disk. It is also what makes the sweep work as designed.
- **`just clean-targets` and `just prune-worktrees`, kept separate.** Stripping
  `target/` is always safe — kache refills it. Removing a worktree is safe only
  once the work is merged, which is why it is the gate's to run. Collapsing them
  makes the safe one inherit the unsafe one's ceremony.
- **kache is given room.** It has been the `RUSTC_WRAPPER` since `mise.toml:24`
  and it is running over budget: **71.4 GiB in a 50 GiB store, 143%**, hit rate
  57%, misses eating 93.7% of wrapper time. `doctor` passes every check — the
  budget is simply too small. Raised to 150 GiB out of the space the worktrees
  give back, then `gc`, then the daemon installed as a service rather than left
  on demand, because four concurrent lanes are exactly what an on-demand daemon
  has not been tested for.
- **Every lane brief carries `RCAD_STEP_CORPUS`.** Without it four `rcad-step`
  tests fail — by §44.10's decision, so that green means the corpus ran — and a
  lane that runs `just default` without the variable reads a red suite as its own
  doing. It is not in the tree (375 MB of third-party files) and it is not in
  `mise.toml` (a machine-specific absolute path), so the only place left is the
  brief. Four lanes hitting the same unexplained failure is four debugging
  sessions for a variable.
- **The heredoc ban is enforced by a hook rather than recorded again.** §49.5
  found three of thirteen lanes patching `.rs` files with heredocs or `sed -i`
  and chose to record it; recording has now been tried and changed nothing. The
  stated risk is that *a pattern that does not match fails quietly*, and quiet
  failure is what a gate reading a diff is worst at catching.

### 50.9 What the two unmerged branches were worth, audited rather than assumed

§50.2 item 5 settled `m5-predicates-scaling`: already in main, byte for byte.
`rcad-fuzz` needed reading, because main fixed the same overflow by a **different
route** and a diff cannot tell a superseded fix from a missing one. Merge base
`67a6b7f`; `rcad-geom` has grown ~17 300 lines since.

**Dead, and the reason matters more than the verdict.** The branch's headline —
*"an axis whose direction was too big to square stored no direction"* — is fixed
on main **twice over**, and the branch's own fix would be unreachable code there.
`normalized_as` measures at a rescaled copy (`point.rs:363`, via
`power_of_two_that_keeps_the_squares_in_range` at `:267`), so its proposed
`if !length.is_finite()` arm can never fire; and `Axis::new` (`point.rs:513`) no
longer calls the raw path at all. Main's version also fixes the **underflow** end
that the branch declined — its doc said *"a direction too small for it is not"* —
so main is strictly better. Both regression seeds are dead too: the defect they
pin is fixed (`half_space.rs:171-175` names this caller by name), and the seeds
are ChaCha byte-strings that no longer replay the recorded pairs after the
generator drifted. **Every number the branch published is stale**, by 5× to 40×,
because M4 and §33 moved the refusal rates underneath them.

**Live, and one of it is a bug in main.**

1. **The order and scale oracles.** `tests/fuzzing/mod.rs` on main exports exactly
   one oracle. There is **no commutativity oracle anywhere in `rcad-geom`** over
   the fuzz corpus — a swapped-argument `intersect` appears twice in the crate,
   both hand-written. The branch adds two: `intersect(a,b)` against
   `intersect(b,a)`, and the same pair written at `2^±1`. That closes a hole the
   branch states plainly — a pair the fuzzer *refuses* to name produces no point
   to check, so every defect that shows up as a refusal was outside what any
   amount of fuzzing could see. It is also the oracle that found the branch's own
   fix, so its catch rate is demonstrated rather than argued.
2. **`MEASURED_CASES * factor` is a bare multiply, and in release it wraps.**
   `how_often_naming_a_crossing_refuses.rs:619`, compounded twenty-fold at
   `:309`, and again at `rcad-topo/tests/turning_a_fuse.rs:318-325`. A soak that
   overflows runs **fewer** cases than shipped while the operator reads the
   number as the wide one — a green run that says nothing, which is §48.2's
   whole subject. `checked_mul` is the fix.
3. **Three files in `rcad-geom` cannot be soaked at all.**
   `how_far_the_marcher_strays…` (96 draws), `every_point_along_a_crossing…`
   (512), `the_same_pair_turned…` (2048) are hard-seeded and hard-sized on main,
   so soaking them reruns the same draws for ever. The branch's defect
   description is **verbatim still true**. Meanwhile `rcad-topo` has grown to
   *three* private copies of the same two variable names, so the argument for one
   shared module is stronger now than when it was written.
4. **`is_on_a_knife_edge` has no `[Sphere, Cylinder]` arm**
   (`the_same_pair_turned…:212`). A ball tangent along a whole circle inside a
   pipe falls through to `_ => false`, so that property reads as covering more
   than it does. Re-derive the case by hand; do not re-add the dead seed. The
   oracle lane deliberately omits a *turn* oracle citing exactly this gap, so
   closing it unblocks a third.

**Two lanes, not one, and they are split by write set rather than by theme.**
Items 2, 3 and 4 all touch the fixed-seed test files, so they are one lane; the
oracles are another. **Lane E may not write
`how_often_naming_a_crossing_refuses.rs`** — that file is Lane F's, and it is the
one file on the branch that conflicts hard, because main rewrote its whole
constants block for M4/§33. Take main's constants wholesale and redo the
private-helper deletion by hand.

**What Lane E must re-derive rather than inherit**, per §50.5's rule applied to a
branch instead of a spike: the branch's `scaled()` and `kind_of()` predate
`Surface::Cone` and `Surface::Torus`, so without new arms they will **silently
skip every cone and torus pair** — a green oracle over a shrinking family, which
is the §48.2 failure again. And its three published floors were measured against
the old surface set; they move.

### 50.10 The prediction

**§49.7's prediction is carried into this unit and scored by charge 2** — a
correct fix that carries a rounded test into a place where it decides an answer.
It is not restated as this unit's own; a prediction scored by the gate that
inherits it is the point.

**The prediction for the unit after this one comes from what this planning session
did wrong twice.** Both times, a plan was made about the tree without reading the
part of the tree that already answered it: a producer and its consumer were put in
concurrent lanes with the dependency unnoticed until a second pass, and a build
cache was proposed as future work while the same tool sat configured in
`mise.toml` and had since 2026-09-02. §49.8 closed on the same shape from the
other end — an expression in a third copy, guarded rather than removed.

> **The next unit will build something the tree already has, somewhere else.**
> Score it by asking, at the next gate, of every new function: was there already
> one, and what search would have found it? The countermeasure is the cheap one —
> grep before writing, not after review.

### 50.11 The spike passed, and it moved the work it was written for

**Pass. 80 000 pairs, 0 undecided, 0 disagreements**, over four draws of 20 000
with slopes and radii spanning `1e-4 … 1e4` each, so the circle standoff
`r/(s·√W)` spanned sixteen decades. Every decision came from level 2 or level 3.

**The claim it was sent to demonstrate is wrong, and in a useful direction.**
`error.rs:331-335` says the coaxial cases are *"one sign question apiece"*. There
is **no shape question at all**: a `Cone` is double-napped (`cone.rs:20-34`) and a
`Cylinder` has a positive radius, so `slope·|h| = ρ` has exactly two roots
`h = ±ρ/slope`. It is **always exactly two circles** — never zero, never one, and
the sphere-and-pipe row's `Pos/Zero/Neg` table has no analogue here. The two signs
that *are* asked decide whether the pair is **coaxial**, and there are two, not
one: `‖w_cone × w_pipe‖² = 0` and `‖(apex − o_pipe) × w_pipe‖² = 0`. Both are sums
of squares, so both answer only `Pos` or `Zero`, and both are shapes
`where_two_pipes_cross:853` already asks. **Nothing new needs deriving**, which is
§50.10's prediction pointing at a lane before the lane ran.

**§50.2 item 4 was right to flag the hazard and wrong that it applies here.**
`assemble.rs:2118` asks *does this crossing hold a straight line*, and **both**
answers to the coaxiality sign give the same answer to it — a quartic holds no
line, and two circles hold no line either. The arm stays `Some(false)`, now under
a proof about geometry instead of about `intersect`'s refusal. So **Lane C's
`assemble.rs` work is a comment, not a door**, and no `Policy`-free export is
needed at all — unlike §49.8's pair. Lane C is thin again and takes its weight
from the pin below instead.

**A limit, total and deferred.** 20 000 of 20 000 apexes built as `origin + t·ŵ`
on a **non-coordinate** axis land off the stored line and are refused. Worst miss
`2.6e-14` on coordinates of order 100 — one or two ulps — and the exact predicate
is *right*: those surfaces genuinely are not coaxial. A limit, not a gap (§16.10).

**Then the corpus was asked whether any of this is worth doing, and the first
answer was no.** Across all 367 files, `ACrossingBetweenAConeAndAnotherCurvedSurface`
is raised **zero times**, and naming the coaxial pair moves the import rate by
**exactly zero files**. Never blended, per §15.10: kicad holds a cone in 9 of 323
files and a coaxial cone-pipe neighbour in **6 of 323 (1.9%)**; nist holds one in
**32 of 44 (73%)**, with **1046 of 1162** adjacent cone-pipe edges exactly
coaxial. All 38 of those files refuse for something else — 26 of nist's 32 die in
the *reader*, on `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` and `VERTEX_LOOP`, before geometry is
asked at all.

Two findings inside that measurement are worth keeping. **Every coaxial pair in
both corpora — 24 of 24 kicad, 2190 of 2190 nist — sits on a coordinate
direction**, which is the spike's limit confirmed from the other side and makes
the count robust. And **nothing anywhere shares an `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` between a
cone and a cylinder** — zero pairs, both corpora — so the expected "they qualify
because the exporter reused a placement" is simply false. About 5% of nist's real
countersinks sit on leaning axes and stay refused even with Lane A.

**But the importer was the wrong place to look, and §48.7 had already said so.**
`crates/rcad-topo/tests/how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs:366` pins
`AFrustumAgainstABar` and `TwoFrustumsOnOneAxis` at `answered == 0`, with the
reason written into the assertion: *"a cone against another curved surface is a
degree-four space curve nothing here can name."* `a_frustum` builds on
`Cone::new(Axis::z(), slope)` (`tests/cones/mod.rs:49`) and the bar is translated
along `z` alone (`:207-213`), so **`AFrustumAgainstABar` is a coaxial cone and
pipe on a coordinate axis — precisely the case the spike decided 20 000 times out
of 20 000.**

- **`AFrustumAgainstABar` is Lane A's named consumer**, and §13 is satisfied by it
  rather than by any file.
- **`TwoFrustumsOnOneAxis` is not.** It is cone against cone (`:216-219`), which
  §50.2 item 4 keeps out of scope, and it stays pinned at zero.
- **The pin at `:366` has to move, and no lane owned that file.** Lane A landing
  makes that assertion *fail*, which is the correct behaviour of a pin and the
  reason it was written. `how_often_a_fuse_with_a_cone_refuses.rs` is added to
  **Lane C's** write set, and splitting the two families' expectations apart is
  what Lane C is for now that its door turned into a comment.

**So Lane A stands, with its claim rewritten and its consumer named.** What it
must not claim is an import-rate gain: there is none, and §50.5's failure
criterion for Lane A is extended to say so — a lane that reports this work as
moving the corpus has reported a number the measurement above already refutes.

## 51. What the endless bend cost and found, recorded 2026-09-05

*Written after the wave, from two closing gates' verdicts rather than from the
lane reports. Where a gate and a lane disagreed, both numbers are given and the
one that was re-derived from the tree wins. Seventeen lanes across four waves,
fifty-two commits, `just default` green twice at the end.*

### 51.1 The sentence, and which half was earned

> **The fuse can put points in order along a curve that never ends, and a cone
> coaxial with a pipe is cut by it.**

**Both of §50.3's falsifiers are satisfied.** `HowItRuns` has a third variant,
`AlongABend`, with a construction site that is not a test; `intersect` no longer
refuses the coaxial pair, and `walk` draws the two circles.

**The consumer the unit was built to prove still answers nothing.**
`AFrustumAgainstABar` is 0 of 96, because the fuse now gets past `intersect` and
stops one step later — *where three surfaces meet is only worked out when two of
them are flat*, and a cone, a pipe and a cap plane give one flat surface. §50.6
puts `three_surfaces.rs` out of scope, so this is the next wall and not a gap in
the work. The pin now carries the new reason and fails the day that wall moves,
which is the only thing that makes a pin holding at zero worth keeping.

### 51.2 Four defects nobody planned for, and what each was hiding behind

None of these is the headline. All four came from a lane or a gate contradicting
the brief it was given.

1. **A fuse refused solids that provably have volume.** `nest_the_shells` decided
   *solid or cavity* on the sign of a rounded sum of triple products —
   `signed_volume` accumulating `a.dot(b.cross(c))` in plain `f64`, with no
   `Decision`, no `Interval` and no exact fallback anywhere on the path. A prism
   over a triangle three ulps off its own long side, whose area `orient2d` proves
   `Pos`, measured `-2.3129646346357427e-18`: **2020 of 20 000 draws refused for
   having no volume.** A square rod `1e-9` across down the `(1,1,1)` diagonal,
   corners as well conditioned as a cube's, measured `-4.5e-18` of `1e-18`.
   Fixed by keeping the rounded sum when a forward bound proves its own sign and
   adding the fan up in `expansion` arithmetic when it does not.

   **Why the existing defence never covered it, proved rather than observed.**
   Every term of a 3×3 determinant carries exactly one factor from each axis, so
   shrinking an axis by a power of two shrinks every term by that power and the
   sum returns bit for bit what it was, scaled. That is what makes `axis_shifts`
   free, and it is the same fact that makes it useless against cancellation: it
   rescues a solid thin along an **axis** and does nothing for one thin along a
   **diagonal**. The guard is also downstream of the decision it would protect —
   `check_dynamic_range` is twenty-three lines and one conditional after
   `nest_the_shells` has already believed the sign.

2. **One surface, two names, from a signed zero — three surfaces in a row.** The
   kernel states *two faces that are the same surface hold the same numbers* in
   four places — `Surface::how_it_sorts_against`, `name_of_surface_bits`,
   `canonical_cut_surfaces`, §32.5 — and all four compare with `total_cmp`, where
   `-0.0 < 0.0`. It enforced it in none. A shared wall put a corner in two places
   one ulp apart. Fixed at construction in `Plane`, then `Axis`, then `Sphere`,
   each by the lane fixing the one before it, each stopping at its write-set
   boundary and handing back rather than reaching. `HalfSpace` is exempt by
   §33.8 — it has no canonical form at all.

   Two measurements worth keeping. Normalization folds **none** of it and can
   **manufacture** a negative zero: a component small enough to underflow against
   the largest (`-5e-324` beside `1e300`) comes out `-0.0` where nothing in the
   input was a zero. And the way in is not exotic — **93 corpus files hold a
   `DIRECTION` with a `-0.` component**, spellings like
   `DIRECTION('',(-0.0,-0.0000000001,-1.0))`, which `direction_at` puts straight
   into `Vector::new` and `placement_at` hands to `Axis::new`.

3. **A soak that reported 4.29 billion cases and ran 2049.** `MEASURED_CASES *
   factor` as a bare multiply, in five places across two crates. In release it
   wraps, so the run is silently narrower than shipped while the operator reads
   the wide number — §48.2's subject, in the machinery built to answer §48.2.
   `checked_mul` throughout, each site demonstrated wrapping before it was fixed.

4. **A soak that could not soak.** Once the multiply was fixed,
   `the_same_pair_turned…` still died at `FACTOR=50` on proptest's
   `max_global_rejects`, a flat 1024 whatever the case count, **before any
   assertion about geometry ran**. Scaled to proptest's own four-per-case ratio;
   ten seeds now compare 2.05 million turned pairs.

### 51.3 The fuzz corpus had stopped growing with the kernel

`two_surfaces_from` reads two bits per surface and asks `which % 3`, so the
824-seed corpus has only ever held planes, balls and pipes — decoded and matched
on `Surface`: **232 planes, 423 balls, 831 pipes, 0 cones, 0 tori**. Bits 4 to 7
of the kinds byte are read by nothing, and `3 % 3` aliases to a plane, so the
draw is 2:1:1 and not uniform. Every claim in the crate that says *over the fuzz
corpus* was a claim about three of five surface kinds.

**The corpus is not repacked, and the second reason is the load-bearing one.**
Promoting the unread bits reinterprets 92 of 824 minimised seeds — not "every one
of them", which is what the file said. But a torus reads eight numbers where a
pipe reads seven, so a torus against a cone, a pipe or another torus needs **76
bytes and the longest seed checked in is 71**. Those pairs would decode to
nothing whatever the kind bits said. Widening the decoder is a lane of its own
and wants the corpus re-minimised with it.

Two oracles landed meanwhile — `intersect(a,b)` against `intersect(b,a)`, and the
same pair written at `2^±1` — closing a hole the tree had no way to see: **a pair
the fuzzer refuses to name produces no point to check**, so every defect that
shows up as a refusal was outside what any amount of fuzzing could reach. Cones
and tori are covered by a separate hand-written table of 136 pairs on the integer
lattice, reported as its own row and never blended (§17.7).

### 51.4 Six false sentences, every one beside a number that was right

This is the unit's finding about itself, and it is §47.8's shape for the fourth
consecutive unit.

| the sentence | what was actually true |
|---|---|
| §50.5: the frustum family answers **84 of 84** | §49.6's 84 was configurations on which a **rule** held, never answers. Pre-wave: 38 answered. Post-wave: **53**, with 0 refused for want of an order where 44 were, and all 31 remaining stopped in `select.rs` |
| §50.2 item 4: naming beyond the coaxial pair is unsafe **because of cone-against-cone** | a **non-coaxial cone and pipe can share a line** — a pipe of radius 2 about `(1,0,1)` through `(0,2,0)` holds the ruling `(t,0,t)` of `Cone::new(Axis::z(), 1.0)`, since `‖(p−o)×d‖² = 8 = 4‖d‖²`. Two families rest on `intersect`'s refusal, not one |
| a lane report: the parabola knife edge is **not reachable with rational numbers** through the public door | `E` is homogeneous of degree 2 in `n`, so normalizing divides it by `L²` and moves no sign, and the division rounds exactly at **power-of-two ratios**. `Cone::new(Axis::z(), 0.5)` against `Plane::from_point_and_normal((0,0,4), (−1,0,0.5))` is a parabola with whole-number points |
| `NO_POINT_MAY_USE_ALL_OF_ITS_BOUND`: the worst a search finds is about **3·ε** against a published 256·ε | true of three planar rows. The quartic control sits at **0.738 of its bound**, about 189·ε; the headline 0.429, the band 0.477 and rising with corpus width |
| the fuzz file: repacking would reinterpret **every one** of the 824 seeds | **92**, or 42 for the narrower repack |
| `plane.rs`, mine: turning a wall round twice is the plane it started as, **bit for bit** | false for a plane storing `-0.0`, which my own fix had just made possible |

Two of the six were written into §50 before any lane ran, and both were the same
error: **quoting a row from an earlier section without opening what it measured.**
§50's preamble says every file and line it cites was checked against the tree by
opening the file. That was true of the file citations and false of the numeric
ones, and the distinction is the whole finding.

### 51.5 §49.7's prediction fired, on one site

> *"The next unit will ship a correct fix that carries a rounded test into a place
> where it decides an answer."*

**Fired, on the presort and only there.** Six of the seven call sites the ordering
predicate reached carry their own derivations and hold up under reading. The
seventh — the hint sort in `nodes_along`, which the building lane's own table
omitted — is a rounded `total_cmp` justified by a sentence inherited verbatim from
the straight-crossing case: *"every neighbouring pair is then proved."* It was
not. `merge_points_that_are_one_point` asked and acted **only on `Decision::Zero`**,
discarding a `Neg`. A gate swapped one pair in the hint and got **8 tests failing
with wrong answers, not refusals**.

Nobody could make the rounded key actually wrong — instrumented, the topo suite
stays green at soak factor 8 with 1024 proptest cases, and the instrument fires
immediately when inverted. So there was no demonstrated defect and no proof
either, and the sentence claimed one.

**The fix is not the assertion the gate proposed**, and the reason belongs in the
record. The hint is a rounded read of the **caller's** coordinates, so asserting
on it puts caller data into a panic; and `order_along` is holding the right answer
at that exact line, which makes it §16.10's **gap** — refusing over an answer
already in hand is the family the rule names. `prove_the_hinted_order` turns the
hint into the order by insertion sort over the proved comparison. The gate's swap
experiment, re-run against the fix, changes nothing: 586 of 586 pass with the hint
deliberately scrambled, for straight crossings and for bends.

### 51.6 The prediction for the next unit

Six sentences, four consecutive units, and the countermeasures already tried are
§15.10's case list (works), the fail-condition brief (works), and the closing gate
(works — it caught five of the six). What none of them reaches is a sentence
written **before** the work, in the planning section, quoting an earlier unit.

> **The next unit's largest error will be inherited from a section it quotes, not
> produced by a lane.** Score it at the next gate by taking every number §51 or
> the next planning section cites from an earlier §, opening what that § actually
> measured, and checking the reading. The countermeasure is cheap and specific:
> **a planning section may not cite a number from an earlier section without
> naming the test or command that produced it.** A row that cannot name one is
> quoted as prose, not as a bound.

### 51.7 What stands, and what this unit made more likely dirty

| open | where |
|---|---|
| **`three_surfaces.rs` wants two flat surfaces** | the new wall for `AFrustumAgainstABar`, 96 of 96, pinned with its reason. §50.6 kept it out |
| **one pipe, two names, from an axis written either way** | `Cylinder::new(Axis::z(), 2.0)` and `Cylinder::new(Axis::z().reversed(), 2.0)` are one surface whose names differ in three of nine numbers. `three_planes_faced_the_one_way` canonicalises this for planes and hands any triple with a curved surface over untouched — deliberately, with a reason about a plane's reversal that is **silent about a curved surface's axis**. Same "one surface, two names" class as §51.2 item 2, different mechanism, unfixed |
| **a mis-signed shell reaching `nest_the_shells`** | both families that flip the sign refuse earlier in the arrangement. Neither barrier is principled — the rod's union answered at `1e-6` and `1e-7` — so it is unproven in both directions. The fix removes the question rather than settling it |
| **`how_much_space_a_curved_solid_encloses`** | in `validate.rs`, still compares refinements against a rounded `f64`. The sign it reads is now exact; the comparison is not audited |
| **the fuzz decoder draws 3 of 5 kinds** | §51.3. Wants the corpus re-minimised with it |
| **`cuts.rs` and most of `three_surfaces.rs`** | still **unaudited**, and now **more likely dirty than before**. §49.8's class was found a fifth time this unit, in the file next door. A comparison-operator grep over both is nearly empty — and that is not evidence, because **it is the same grep that missed the volume sign**, where the rounded sum sat three call-levels away behind a function returning `f64`. Whatever audits them must follow every `f64`-returning call |
| **`ResultIsNotManifold` with `count` other than 1** | unchanged, and now with 9 named draws from the `AFrustumAgainstABlock` family |
| **the writer, fillets, the torus, cone against cone** | unchanged |

### 51.8 What was learned about running the work

- **Five lanes at once, then three, three and one.** Write sets were named before
  any lane started and every merge was clean — no conflict in seventeen lanes.
  The cost of that discipline is that a lane which finds a defect one file outside
  its set must hand it back; the benefit is that four of them did, and each
  handback became the next lane's whole deliverable.
- **Briefs that name what counts as *failing* keep working.** Third unit running.
  Every one of §51.4's corrections came from a lane or gate contradicting its own
  brief — which only happens if the brief says what a wrong answer would look like.
- **Two gates, split by numbers and by claims, beat one gate.** Each found things
  the other did not, and each disagreed with a lane. A gate is also not exempt:
  the claims gate published corpus kind counts that did not sum to `743 × 2`, and
  the lane that re-derived them said so and showed the arithmetic.
- **A `sonnet` lane staged its whole deliverable and never committed it.** The
  brief said commit as you go; had it been killed, all of it was lost. Worth a
  hook rather than another sentence in a brief, on §50.8's reasoning that
  recording a rule has been tried.
